items.text:
LONDON COLNEY, England -- Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said he hopes the wait to learn Manchester City's punishment for breaking Premier League rules does not overshadow Sunday's meeting between the two sides and urged the Gunners to win the title on the pitch regardless.
City were found guilty on 114 counts of breaching financial regulations over a nine-year period to 2018 but continue to protest their innocence.
They have appealed the verdicts with an outcome expected in December or January but at present, City face a range of punishments including expulsion from the league, a points deduction and a huge fine.
City are currently odds-on with bookmakers to be relegated from the Premier League this season, putting a strange complexion on what would otherwise be a big game between two title challengers at Emirates Stadium.
Asked whether the wait to learn City's fate overshadowed the match in any way, Arteta said: "I hope that it doesn't because as well this is a process that is still open, it is not resolved and we don't know what is going to happen.
"I think when we have two teams at the level that they are both at right now with the quality players they have on that pitch, it is a massive game and a big game to enjoy I think."
Arsenal could open up a nine-point gap over City with a victory and pushed on whether he wanted his team to ensure they didn't rely on a point deduction and win the title on the pitch, Arteta replied: "That's the only thing that we should put the energy and focus in, there is nothing else."
Arteta tight-lipped over Raya's injury recovery
Arteta was evasive when asked whether David Raya would be fit to face City. Raya missed Wednesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund due to a shoulder problem but was pictured at the game without any sling or shoulder support.
Arteta suggested Raya was training but refused to confirm if the Spaniard would be available.
"I don't know," he said. "We still have a few hours before the game. We're still trying to get everyone back."

José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League
items.text:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, continuing his superb start to the season.
The midfielder's form has helped Madrid keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the LaLiga table, with a three-point gap between the pair going into this weekend's games.
"I don't like to compare players from different generations," Mourinho said in a news conference on Friday when asked to rank Bellingham with Zidane.
"Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare."
Mourinho rested Bellingham for the first half against PSV, only to see his team struggle and go 1-0 down -- and the coach responded by sending on Bellingham at halftime to turn the match around.
Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé are two of the Madrid players who have featured most in LaLiga this season, with 1047 and 1163 minutes respectively.
"The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule," Mourinho said. "It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude."
- Jude Bellingham: I don't care about the Ballon d'Or
- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'
The victory over PSV left Madrid top of the Champions League table on 15 points from five games, but Mourinho wouldn't accept that his side are now among the favourites to win the competition. "It's very early," Mourinho said. "We don't know how the teams will arrive at the key moment, the knockout. Right now the only thing I want is not to play the playoffs.
Mourinho said Trent Alexander-Arnold was unavailable to face Alavés on Saturday with illness, while he insisted that he doesn't want to add to his squad in the January window.
"I don't want anyone to come in, or anyone to leave," Mourinho said. "The door is closed in both ways... I don't want to see news about the market, because I don't want anyone."

items.text:
Ronaldo has said that Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or was "well deserved" and that he was delighted to see a fellow No. 9 win the award.
The Brazil legend, who won the Ballon d'Or in 1997 and again in 2002, announced Kane as the winner at the star-studded event at the London Palladium last month.
The 33-year-old England captain starred for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga and the Champions League and led his country to the World Cup semifinals, scoring 73 goals in the process. He is the fifth English player to receive the honour and the first since Michael Owen in 2001.
Kane beat the likes of Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the prestigious award. He is the first recognised striker to win the Ballon d'Or since Karim Benzema in 2022.
Speaking on the Stick to Football podcast on Disney+, Ronaldo said: "It was nice and well deserved for him, I think.
"And I was happy for him and for me too because the No. 9 is back. I'm so happy. [It's been a] long time without the No. 9 winning something important. And then he's also very nice guy. So well deserved. I was very, very happy for him."
Asked by Jamie Carragher how important the award is in Brazil in comparison to in England, Ronaldo said: "Well, for us it's very important. Everywhere it's important. Maybe in England because you won only with Michael Owen last time, now it's important again with Harry Kane.
"But I think it's very important to the players to get together and talk about the last season, what they did. There is still not transparency about how the criteria to put the best players in the world. We know that the captains vote and the journalists vote, but for sure he's the best striker."
Kane has since torn a ligament in his left ankle and is aiming for a return at the "business end of the season."
Ronaldo's brilliant career is synonymous with two major knee injuries, the second of which occurred just six minutes into his comeback and sidelined him for over a year. He said he thinks modern-day strikers have it "much easier" than his generation did.
"I wish I had protection in that time," he said. "We suffered so much in that time. In our generation was killers, killers everywhere. Everywhere I played so many killers and we are not protected. Now, thank God, they are very protected and it's fair.
"I just regret I didn't have that protection in my time."

items.text:
Serbia’s student-led movement nominates chemistry professor for presidency
Radomir Saicic, who teaches at Belgrade University, was among the first university professors to join the student-led protest movement.
Serbia’s student-backed movement, which won an October election after rallying against corruption, has named university professor Radomir Saicic as its presidential candidate in next month’s polls.
Saicic, who teaches chemistry at Belgrade University, is a member of the newly elected parliament as a representative of the Student List, which won 140 seats in the 250-member parliament.
The role is largely ceremonial, but the president is responsible for nominating prime ministers and serves as commander-in-chief of the armed forces.
The December 27 presidential vote comes after Aleksandar Vucic – who dominated Serbian politics for 14 years – cut short his second presidential term to run for prime minister but was soundly defeated by the student-led movement in the parliamentary ballot.
Speaking at a televised news conference in Belgrade on Friday, Saicic said the movement must now prioritise strengthening the rule of law and fighting corruption.
“Now we have the opportunity to turn the freedom we fought for into lasting change,” he said.
“The assembly, the government and the courts must once again earn the trust of the people. The same applies to the institution of the president.”
Saicic pledged a “sovereign Serbia in which the constitution will be respected and in which every citizen will be able to live with dignity”.
Saicic, 65, is also a member of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, and was among the first university professors to join the student-led protest movement that emerged in 2024.
He said he was proud that students trusted him enough to put him forward as a presidential candidate, adding that “the last decade was marred by the crumbling of the rule of law, corruption and hate speech”.
“The outgoing regime is still trying to disintegrate our state,” he said. “In order to prevent this, we need to restore the institutions.”
Vucic, now an opposition member of parliament, has repeatedly suggested his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) might sit out the election, but a final decision is expected in mid-December.
Vucic himself is barred from running again as the constitution limits presidents to two terms.
The parliamentary and presidential elections followed nearly two years of protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
The disaster at the recently renovated station, widely blamed on corruption, triggered Serbia’s largest protests since the fall of strongman Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.
The movement’s initial demand for a transparent investigation evolved into calls for snap elections, which Vucic eventually announced after nearly two years of resistance.

items.title: John Simpson: Ukraine is bowed but still unbroken as freezing weather sets in
items.summary:
Something weird happens when you reach Kyiv after the eight-hour drive from the Polish border: the clock on your mobile phone goes to midnight. It's not really for phones - it seems to be part of a wider strategy to disorient the missiles and drones the Russians are sending over.
Aside from little t
items.text:
Something weird happens when you reach Kyiv after the eight-hour drive from the Polish border: the clock on your mobile phone goes to midnight. It's not really for phones - it seems to be part of a wider strategy to disorient the missiles and drones the Russians are sending over.
Aside from little things like that, though, Kyiv seems fairly normal at first sight. You become well aware there's a war on when sirens begin to wail and people check their phones for the notifications which tell them there's a red alert and missiles are on their way. You can even buy gadgets that show you which direction the drones are coming from, and what type they are.
The drones and ballistic missiles have been hitting in sizeable numbers over the last couple of weeks. On the morning of Monday 16 November, the battle of the bridges began. Ukraine hit the Kerch bridge which links Russia to illegally occupied Crimea. Then it launched a bigger wave of missiles and drones, damaging the central road-bridge arch. A few hours later, presumably in revenge, Russia fired seven ballistic missiles at Kyiv, disabling two of the nine bridges that cross the River Dnipro.
The war has dragged on for more than four and a half years, killing what some estimate could be 100,000 Ukrainian troops and 18,000 Ukrainian civilians, according to the United Nations, and probably more. Its infrastructure, too, has been battered, as well as its morale. While temperatures drop to freezing at night, and with Ukrainians regularly suffering from no light, heat or water thanks to Russian strikes, can the country survive another difficult winter under bombardment? And what would a peace deal, if one could be struck, look like?
Surviving blackouts
Kyiv is mostly dark at night, thanks to Russia's campaign of targeting Ukraine's electricity generating capability. In the blackness last week, the air raid sirens started wailing across the city, and our hotel's warning announcements came over the loudspeakers. Within a few minutes, we heard the first explosions. I jumped out of bed and stared out of the window into the darkness. After a few seconds two more missiles landed, lighting up the entire sky momentarily in a blaze of white and red. They were uncomfortably close.
Many people prefer to go to the shelters when there's a red alert. Others just stay in bed and hope the law of averages will protect them. It usually does. During one of the heaviest attacks last week, the number of fatalities was in single figures.
I went to the shelter in our hotel one night. The clearly audible thumps and crashes above ground, the permanent lighting, the snores and grunts of other people, and the attentions of the little biting flies that seem to thrive in the warm, crowded shelters made sleep hard.
To the people who live here in Kyiv, it's frightening, certainly, if a drone or a missile hits close by, but enraging too. Over the years I've been in several cities that were being bombed by high-tech weaponry and the reaction always seems the same, whether it's Lebanon, Iraq, Serbia, or Ukraine: a combination of weariness and fury. In Kyiv the attacks come by night and day, making normal life almost impossible. An uninterrupted night's sleep is a rarity. The morning after the bridges were hit, people in the streets looked tired and worn.
Yet although they long for it to stop, there's no sign they want Ukraine to surrender. On the contrary, just about everyone I spoke to felt they had to keep fighting. That's borne out by an opinion poll last month by the KIIS organisation, a Ukrainian market research company, which found that 62% of people were prepared to put up with the war for as long as it took. Of those polled, 79% believed that Ukraine would win the war in the long run, and only 7% thought Russia would win. These aren't the reactions of a country which is being beaten to its knees.
Raving through the war
I don't have any doubt that Ukraine can survive the winter. Food is plentiful, though prices are high. Water is a problem, because the regular attacks on the power grid mean that it can't be pumped with any regularity. Kyiv underwent a large transformation under the Soviets, so there are large numbers of high-rise blocks of flats everywhere. Labouring up and down the stairs when there's no power is daunting, especially when you've got to carry quantities of water home.
We came across a small crowd of people in their 20s who had gathered outside a nightclub for a rave at three in the afternoon, because of the 11pm curfew. "It's a way of getting a bit of respite from everything," said one young woman. "It makes me feel I can put up with everything," said a man.
Do people still support President Volodymyr Zelensky? My team and I met an elderly woman wandering around Independence Square in the centre of Kyiv holding a photo of her son, who was missing on the Eastern front. She blamed Zelensky; if he didn't insist on carrying on the war, she believed, her son would still be alive. It isn't a response most people seem to share. The same polling organisation, KIIS, found that Zelensky's trust ratings hover around 54% to 57% — way below the 90% he was registering in the early days of the war in 2022, but not too bad for a man who's been in power now for more than seven years.
What comes across all the time in Kyiv is an absolute loathing of Russia. Putin reportedly launched his invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 because his intelligence chiefs assured him that Ukrainians longed to rejoin the Motherland.
Russian missiles have hit hospitals, clinics and schools. In many well-attested cases the Russians have used the "double-tap" method — sending in one missile, then waiting till the medics and rescuers gather before sending in another. At least 20,000 Ukrainian children have been abducted and taken to Russia, according to Ukraine's Ministry of Justice. items.summary:
Canada’s top court largely upholds Quebec’s religious symbols ban
Quebec’s ban on teachers and police wearing religious symbols such as hijabs and turbans at work remains in place.
A landmark ruling by Canada’s Supreme Court has largely upheld Quebec’s secularism law, leaving in place a ban on publi
items.text:
Canada’s top court largely upholds Quebec’s religious symbols ban
Quebec’s ban on teachers and police wearing religious symbols such as hijabs and turbans at work remains in place.
A landmark ruling by Canada’s Supreme Court has largely upheld Quebec’s secularism law, leaving in place a ban on public school teachers, police officers and some other public employees wearing religious symbols at work.
The court ruled on Friday that requiring elected members of Quebec’s National Assembly to uncover their faces infringes upon their democratic rights. That part of the law cannot be enforced against them.
The court also weighed in on a question that goes beyond Quebec — how far governments can go in using the notwithstanding clause.
The clause is part of Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms. It lets federal and provincial legislators keep a law in force even if it violates certain Charter rights, including freedom of religion and the right to equality, shielding it from court challenges. The override lasts up to five years and can be renewed. Quebec used it when it passed Bill 21 in 2019 and renewed it in 2024.
On Friday, the Supreme Court said politicians can use the clause without waiting for a court to rule on whether a law violates Charter rights. It also said judges can still declare that a law violates those rights, as judges in lower courts had done, even if the clause keeps the law in force.
What the law does
Quebec passed Bill 21 in June 2019, saying it would protect the religious neutrality of public institutions. It bars people in certain public jobs from wearing religious symbols such as hijabs, turbans and kippahs while at work. Teachers who were already in their posts on March 27, 2019, were able to continue wearing them as long as they stayed in the same role with the same employer.
The law has reshaped lives, leading to people losing their jobs and leaving Quebec to avoid the restrictions. Some Muslim women have decided to take off their hijabs while at work in order to be able to keep their jobs.
Quebec has since widened the restrictions to support staff and volunteers at school, as well as daycare workers.
How the case reached the court
Quebec invoked the notwithstanding clause when it passed Bill 21, before any court had ruled on the law. The override lasts up to five years and can be renewed. Quebec renewed it in 2024.
A Quebec Superior Court judge upheld most of the law in 2021, but found that it infringed certain rights that the clause cannot override, including the minority-language education rights of English-language school boards. Quebec’s Court of Appeal reversed the exemption for those boards in 2024 and left most of the law in place. Seven Supreme Court justices heard the case over four days in March.

items.title: Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
items.summary:
Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
- Published
Touring musicians from across the US who descended on New York City to perform at the Macy's Thanksgiving parade have turned to fundraising to cover their costs, after getting stuck when the event was rearranged
items.text:
Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
- Published
Touring musicians from across the US who descended on New York City to perform at the Macy's Thanksgiving parade have turned to fundraising to cover their costs, after getting stuck when the event was rearranged due to a storm.
A band from Texas told the BBC's US partner, CBS News, it had raised some $350,000 (£267,000) to pay for an extended stay for its 500 members. It saluted the kindness of its supporters.
A group of student musicians from Hawaii, meanwhile, voiced their relief after friends and family rallied around to cover their additional hotel, coach and meal costs.
The parade, a famous annual event, is now scheduled to take place on Saturday.
Earlier this week, organisers said they would it push it back by two days, in part due to the concerns around flying giant inflatables in strong winds.
The balloons were temporarily deflated for a few days - and so too were the spirits of those who had journeyed to the city to watch the action.
The move represented the first time the event had been postponed, although it was suspended altogether during World War Two.
Each year, a number of marching bands travel from across the country, some of them from high schools, to provide music for the event. This is considered a huge opportunity, as the parade is watched by millions of people in person and on TV.
- Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather 
  - Published1 day ago
The leader of the Texas band described his emotions as costs for his delegation were met.
"It's been exhausting and emotional to figure this out, but it has been incredibly humbling to see an outpouring of kindness," Ryan Demkovich, the director of the Pride of Pearland Marching Band at Pearland High School, near Houston, in Texas, told CBS.
Demkovich said contributions had arrived from businesses and individuals in the band's home community, with the help of a social media push.
Meanwhile, the Hawaii group, the the Nā Koa Aliʻi Hawaiʻi All-State Marching Band, said it would still be able to participate in the parade, as a result of the efforts of families, friends, and other supporters who raised more than $500,000.
Speaking to the BBC earlier on Thursday, the group's director Rickey H Badua described the time pressures. "We are racing to get this done," he explained.
The band is made up of hundreds of musicians from dozens of schools across the state. It had travelled almost 5,000 miles (8,000km) to get to New York.
"Getting the news that we got the parade postponed was not easy, and emotional, for our students," Badua said.
But the musicians sprang into action quickly, he said. "We come from a very far place," Badua said, adding that "to get so close to the finish line and not show up for it, we couldn't give up that easily".
The response from friends and family had been "incredible", he said.
Badua was hopeful his group would get the same experience he had when he first performed in the parade in 2003, as student drum major.
"The energy is palpable, people are just excited to see a band that is great."
Another musical act, from Illinois, told the BBC on Thursday it was trying to raise $175,000 to cover another night in a hotel, additional food, and bus costs back to the city of Champaign.
"Things are going well due to the very generous support of so many amazing human beings," said Prof Barry Houser, director of the University of Illinois Marching Illini.
While awaiting the parade, musicians and punters alike have sheltered from the heavy wind and rain that were brought by a storm to eastern areas of the US.
Hundreds of thousands of homes lost power, and coastal areas were flooded. The National Weather Service (NWS) expects conditions to improve gradually on Friday.
Additional reporting by Jessica Murphy

‘Playing with fire’: Republicans incensed after Trump gets Huang reinstated
Former Trump officials warn his push to reinstate NVIDIA’s CEO could be the final straw for Republicans.
United States President Donald Trump’s involvement in getting NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang reinstated has drawn little support from his own party with some Republican officials warning this could be a blow to the president’s popularity with his conservative base.
Earlier this week, the US president ignited a firestorm across Washington, DC, after he revealed he personally contacted NVIDIA’s board of directors and “convinced” its members to let Huang return.
Trump said he spoke to the board “directly and indirectly” in the less than two weeks between Huang’s resignation and his reinstatement, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The move amounted to an extraordinary intervention by the US president, whose predecessors, both Democratic and Republican, have largely avoided personally involving themselves – or their administrations – in corporate matters.
“I felt very strongly about it,” Trump told CNBC on Monday about his decision to contact NVIDIA’s board. “And I felt more strongly as I saw what was happening with the … company, because that was, to me, a very important part of our country.”
After Huang’s resignation, shares of NVIDIA, which financial disclosures show Trump holds tens of millions of dollars of stock in, dropped sharply, wiping out more than $1tn in market value. They rebounded after Huang was reinstated.
A White House spokesperson told Al Jazeera that “Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions” and neither Trump nor any of his family members has input on how investments are made.
Several Republican lawmakers in the US Senate have publicly objected to Huang’s reinstatement, expressing alarm that China, via the tech executive’s affair, may have obtained access to NVIDIA’s chips for its artificial intelligence arms race against the US. They have not, however, mentioned Trump’s foray into the matter.
“The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” Republican Senator Tom Cotton, a member of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China and the Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, posted to social media. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip-export control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”
US Senate Majority Leader John Thune, who will continue to lead Republicans in the chamber when they enter the minority at the start of the next Congress in January, told Al Jazeera in a statement that Huang’s actions create “a significant national security vulnerability”.
“Through vigorous oversight and adoption of strong, bipartisan export-control measures, Congress will do its part to ensure our national security interests are being met,” Thune said. “The American people expect and deserve no less.”
Trump said NVIDIA’s board sought assurances that Huang did not pose a national security risk because of his relationship with Alice Huang, the former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US officials suspect of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has denied the allegation.
The US president, who said the NVIDIA CEO had been “exonerated”, noted that his assessment aligned with one conducted by the US Department of Justice. But in a news conference on Tuesday, US Attorney General Todd Blanche sidestepped questions about a reported investigation into Huang.
Privately, several former US Republican officials have told Al Jazeera it could be the final straw after a decade with a leader that some in the GOP have said has never been bound by traditional conservative principles.
“How very President Xi of him,” a former Trump administration official, speaking on condition of anonymity to speak candidly, said of the US president’s “communist-esque” actions in getting involved with NVIDIA, likening them to ones taken by the Chinese leader. “I think that sets a dangerous precedent.”
The official, who worked with Trump in the White House during his first term, described the modern-day US Republican Party as a tripod supported by three key values: religion, free market economics and national security.
But after Trump said he intervened with NVIDIA’s board to get Huang back on top, a leg of the “conservative stool,” they said, was broken.
“You need all three to stand. And he just ripped one out,” the official said. “So, at some point, the chair falls.”
“If he’s going to betray national security … why wouldn’t he betray the other legs, you know, on social conservative and economic issues?” they added. “I think it raises a lot of questions for folks and … he’s playing with fire.”
Ashley Davis, a Republican strategist who serves on several corporate boards, said NVIDIA, not Trump, will bear responsibility for reinstating Huang.
“If the president wants to make a phone call, because he’s concerned about chips or concerned about the macroeconomics of the impact of NVIDIA failing, that’s his prerogative,” Davis said. “It’s whether NVIDIA’s board wants to vote that way or not, and they did.”
Next week, Huang is slated to participate in a transcribed interview with the US House Foreign Affairs Committee, as well as a separate public hearing with the Senate Banking Committee.
One of the latter’s Republican members, Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, said he expects Huang will “take the Fifth Amendment so he doesn’t incriminate himself in criminal prosecution.”
“It’s not my place as a senator to tell Mr Huang that he can’t cheat on his wife,” Kennedy told Fox News on Tuesday. “It is my place to tell him if you’re cheating on your wife with somebody who could be a Chinese spy, that jeopardises national security.”

items.title: Renée Slegers leaves job as Arsenal Women’s coach after dismal run of results
items.summary:
Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent.
The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Supe
items.text:
Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent.
The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League this season have left Arsenal sixth, 12 points behind the leaders, Chelsea, and eight points adrift of a European place.
Arsenal’s assistant coach Aaron D’Antino has also left, having been on the backroom staff since 2018. Arsenal’s director of women’s football, Clare Wheatley, told the club’s website a “change was necessary”, saying: “It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renée, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here.
“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renée has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron. After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary.”
Arsenal’s chief executive, Richard Garlick, described Slegers as a “wonderful person” but said a new head coach was required to give the club the best chance of meeting the ambition “to compete for and win major trophies consistently”.
It is understood Arsenal were determined to give Slegers time and so stood by her earlier in the season when speculation about her future was mounting but that eventually the two parties concluded a change was needed.
Arsenal’s search to find Slegers’ replacement is under way but it is understood the club will not rush to make an appointment, because their priority is to find the best person rather than ensuring somebody is in place for their next match, at Everton on 11 December in the WSL.
Melissa Clarke-Reed, the former Brighton and London City Lionesses head coach, has been placed in interim charge. The club are believed to be comfortable with her, if necessary, overseeing the three games that precede the winter break. Arsenal then return to action on 10 January.
Slegers took charge in October 2024, initially as interim head coach, after the resignation of Jonas Eidevall, under whom she had worked as an assistant. She oversaw a run of 10 wins in 11 matches without defeat in caretaker charge, prompting the club to appoint her as the head coach on an 18-month deal.
The Dutchwoman then led Arsenal to one of the greatest moments in their history as they won the Women’s Champions League title on 24 May 2025, stunning Barcelona with a surprise 1-0 victory in Lisbon to record the club’s second European title and their first for 18 years.
The 2025-26 season ended with Arsenal second in the WSL, four points behind the champions, Manchester City. They were semi-finalists in the Champions League and League Cup and quarter-finalists in the FA Cup, but Slegerswon – on home soil – the inaugural Fifa Women’s Champions Cup, a competition between the winners of the respective continental titles.
Arsenal had held high hopes of mounting a WSL title challenge this term, vying to win their first domestic league title since 2019 and had what appeared to be a strong summer transfer window, signing high-calibre internationals such as the England midfielder Georgia Stanway and the Spain full-back Ona Batlle.
They have had injuries, including to their integral midfielder Mariona Caldentey, who is sidelined with a hamstring problem. The team’s inability to break down opponents set up in a low block has been a repetitive issue, and on Sunday there were loud boos at the Emirates when they were held to a goalless draw by West Ham.
Slegers, a former Netherlands midfielder, managed the Swedish club Rosengård and Sweden’s snder-23s before joining Arsenal in 2023 to work under Eidevall.

items.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
items.summary:
Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
- Published
Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the opt
items.text:
Man Utd trigger Fernandes' one-year contract extension
- Published
Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.
It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.
The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.
Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his £47m move from Sporting in January 2020.
Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.
While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.
United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.
After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.
Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.
The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.
"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."
Good, not nice - Pochettino
Pochettino was criticised by former Liverpool and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp on the Overlap earlier this week.
Reference was made to the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea coach high-fiving Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davidson after his side's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, as evidence Pochettino had lost his edge.
"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked like he had that Argentinian dog in him," said Redknapp.
"I look at him now and he's high-fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice."
It seems someone had mentioned the observation to Pochettino as he went off on a tangent at his Friday news conference when asked about a "crazy" first week that included red cards, refereeing errors, disallowed goals and a drone filming training.
"What are we going to do? Start to cry?" he asked. "No. We have to be strong, believe and keep going. I cannot judge the past. Who am I to do that? I was in Cincinnati. I was outside. I need to shut my mouth, say nothing and start from now.
"Sometimes we are so confusing two words that means something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. We have to be good. It is a different thing. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything.
"These two things are different."
Pochettino also confirmed £70m midfielder Carlos Baleba is expected to be out until the last week in January with the hamstring injury he sustained against Roma on 3 November.
Forward Marcus Rashford had begun to do individual work outside as he tries to recover from a hip problem that has kept him out since 13 October.

items.summary:
Manchester United trigger Bruno Fernandes contract extension to 2028
The captain had said that a long-term contract renewal was on hold, but Premier League club exercised one-year option.
Manchester United are understood to have extended Bruno Fernandes’ existing contract by 12 months, ending specul
items.text:
Manchester United trigger Bruno Fernandes contract extension to 2028
The captain had said that a long-term contract renewal was on hold, but Premier League club exercised one-year option.
Manchester United are understood to have extended Bruno Fernandes’ existing contract by 12 months, ending speculation about a pre-contract agreement with an overseas club.
The Professional Football Association’s Player of the Year was in the final year of his existing contract, which would have allowed him to speak with clubs outside the Premier League from January 1 about a move next summer.
Fernandes had revealed that negotiations about a new contract had been put on hold, adding to speculation that he could seek a move away from a team that are currently in the league relegation zone.
United, however, are understood to have triggered a clause in the current deal to keep Fernandes at the Old Trafford club until the end of the 2027-2028 season.
Fernandes joined United in January 2020 from Sporting Lisbon, against whom he scored twice in the two sides’ midweek Champions League 2-2 draw.
The attacking midfielder quickly became the club’s most important player and last season performed a record number of assists in a Premier League season, helping secure the return to Europe’s elite competition for this campaign.
A team source said the move suited both parties and left the door open to future talks over a new contract, although the immediate priority was improving results.
United are languishing in 19th place in the Premier League after their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.
Fernandes a doubt for Manchester United against Brentford
United entertain Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday, marking new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game in charge of the club.
Fernandes, however, is a doubt for the match after missing training on Friday due to illness.
“We don’t know,” Pochettino said on Friday when asked if Fernandes will play. “He’s affected by a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem and today he could not be part of the training session.”
“We’ll see during the day and [Saturday] how he wakes up. We’re not going to take any risks. When this type of situation happens, you don’t feel right. We are going to pay attention, but still we have decided nothing.”
Pochettino is still searching for his first victory after the dramatic draw in Lisbon and a 4-0 Premier League thrashing by Liverpool last weekend, although United were encouraged by their improved display in Portugal.
“We arrive full of energy, positive, but it’s difficult for the players when the results haven’t been up to scratch. We try to help them as best we can,” Pochettino said of his first week in charge.
“This is a group of players who want to do well, who want to perform. Our ‌‌job is to build confidence.”
On the speculation that had been swirling around Fernandes’ future in Manchester, following reports he had turned down two new contract offers, the Portugal midfielder said on Tuesday ‌‌that ‌‌talks could wait until results improve.
“I’m more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position to be proud of,” he said.

items.title: Slegers sacked by Arsenal
items.summary:
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunne
items.text:
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal only 18 months after winning Champions League following poor start to WSL season
Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunners sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off the top and have not won at home in the league all season
Friday 27 November 2026 15:06, UK
Renee Slegers has been sacked as Arsenal head coach after a poor start to the Women's Super League season.
Slegers led Arsenal to Women's Champions League glory in May 2025, having initially stepped up from assistant to Jonas Eidevall on an interim basis, then narrowly missed out on the WSL title to Manchester City in 2025/26.
Such was her success at the time, the Dutchwoman signed a new contract with the club in January 2026, running until 2029.
But a poor start to the 2026/27 campaign, in which Arsenal went on a five-game winless run in the WSL for the first time in their history, has culminated in Slegers' departure just 10 months into her new deal.
- Arsenal booed off after goalless draw with West Ham
- WSL latest news and transfers | FREE WSL highlights
- Got Sky? Watch WSL games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream WSL games with no contract📺
The Gunners remain winless at home in the WSL this season having drawn a sixth consecutive game against West Ham on Sunday.
Arsenal sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off leaders Chelsea and eight points behind London City Lionesses in the third and final Champions League position.
Slegers' side have also only scored 11 goals in 11 WSL matches this season - only Everton and bottom club Charlton have managed fewer this term.
Her assistant coach Aaron D'Antino - who has been with the Gunners since 2018 - also leaves the club, with former Brighton boss and current Arsenal head of analytics Melissa Clarke-Reed taking interim charge.
"It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here," said director of women's football Clare Wheatley.
"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.
"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."
'Lack of WSL title challenge part of decision'
Analysis from Sky Sports News' Uma Gurav: "It was one of those decisions that felt like it was coming, particularly after the last set of games that Arsenal have played.
"This follows Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham at the Emirates last weekend and what's so significant about that is it means Arsenal are yet to win at home in the WSL this season, a place that used to be their fortress.
"Now, it's a place where so many teams have come and taken points off them.
"It just didn't look like a coherent Arsenal team on Sunday. Players were coming off in tears and it means they have a lot of work to do to get anything out of this season.
"At the moment, they are eight points off those Champions League places. They wanted to win the WSL this season - that hasn't happened and I think that's partly why this decision has been taken.
"Arsenal have got three more games before Christmas, all away games at Everton and Charlton in the WSL and then one against Inter Milan to see what they can salvage so far from this block of games.
"When we return from the international break, it will be a new Arsenal, with a new team in charge. Let's see if they can turn their season around."
Slegers' final words as Arsenal boss
Renee Slegers speaking after Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham on if she's considering her future:
"I love the club. I'm very passionate about this group of players, we're going through a very, very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities, because the results haven't been good enough.
"In the second half we are chasing again, but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better. But I take my responsibilities in my role.
"That [fans booing] is on us and that's our responsibility. That it's so quiet in the stadium because we don't inspire enough. We don't bring enough energy.
"I think, about the fans, because it's cold and they want to see good football and get inspired today and that's not what we did. And at the end of the day, that's my responsibility.
"And so that doesn't feel good. The fans booing at the end they care and they want more from this team which the group is determined to turn things around.
"It's very tough for the players and the players that have been at Arsenal for longer, or even the players that came last year, no one has gone through this ever with Arsenal.
"So, of course, I think the group has been great. They've been very good in the situation, but, of course, it's the last one of the block and frustration is expressed, which I don't think is a bad thing, because we shouldn't be accepting this."

items.text:
Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
November 27, 2026
Thailand is pushing its neighbor Myanmar to take on unregulated mining.
A toxic border river is putting lives and livelihoods at risk in northern Thailand. The Kok River, once rich in fish, is now polluted with arsenic, mercury, and other hazardous contaminants.
The reason is the mining activity in the militia-controlled regions of Myanmar. Most of these mines are located in Shan state, where civil war has raged since the 2021 military coup.
The mining activity is driven in part by China's dominant rare earth industry.
Two sides agreed to joint water sampling
Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were the reason of the pollution downstream. China was also present in the talks.
The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This will cover 12 water sampling locations and is expected to begin between December and January.
But no public agreement was made about Thailand's request for a six-month suspension of mining operations.
The talks follow the suspension of tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district earlier this month, near the Myanmar border, after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times higher than government limits.
Bangkok is also seeking China's help in pressuring private Chinese operators, given its position as the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, as the issue grows increasingly urgent after months of concern.
Authorities this week urged residents to avoid eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests detected dangerous levels of arsenic and lead in northern and northeastern Thailand.
Myanmar intervention to stop mining faces obstacles
"Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar's) Shan state, no-one disagrees," Thai Deputy Prime Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said at the joint talks.
However, finding a solution remains a challenge.
Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), told AFP, "This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity.”
But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be "really difficult," he added.
Several ethnic armed groups have been active in the region for decades, while the civil war is still ongoing.
Thai authorities point to two gold mines across the border from Mae Sai as the main contributors to elevated arsenic levels in the Sai River.
The broader region is divided among various groups, including Myanmar's military and the United Wa State Army, an ethnic armed group closely aligned with China.
The main mining belts are currently outside the control of Myanmar's military-backed government, including sites in Shan State.
Thailand might ask China's help, PM says
Thai authorities are also seeking to assess whether pollutant mines are under the control of Myanmar's government or other entities, Deputy Prime Minister Yodchanan told Reuters.
"We also would like them to check whether they can control every mine or they cannot. If they cannot, we will ask China to help,” he said.
A spokesperson from China's foreign ministry told AFP that Beijing "pays close attention" to the pollution issue and would provide technical support.

Soldier Reeves banished doubts about his staying ability with a magnificent display in the Coral Long Distance Hurdle. In the feature race, Dan Skelton's charge proved too good for previous winners Impose Toi
items.text:
Newbury: Dan Skelton's Soldier Reeves emerges as future star with Long Distance Hurdle win
Soldier Reeves banished doubts about his staying ability with a magnificent display in the Coral Long Distance Hurdle. In the feature race, Dan Skelton's charge proved too good for previous winners Impose Toi and Strong Leader - who was gallant in second.
Friday 27 November 2026 16:09, UK
Soldier Reeves emerged as the new kid on the block in the staying division with an impressive comeback victory in the Coral Long Distance Hurdle at Newbury.
Dan Skelton's five-year-old mixed it with the best around in novice hurdles last season, most notably finishing fourth behind King Rasko Grey when upped in trip for the Turners Novices' Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival before finding only high-class stablemate Bossman Jack too strong at Aintree.
He faced another step into the unknown on his reappearance, taking on more hardened stayers on his first start over three miles under rules, but travelled powerfully throughout in the hands of Harry Skelton and was right on the heels of the redoubtable Strong Leader on the approach to the final flight.
The latter did his best to regain his crown, having emerged victorious two years ago and finished a close second to Impose Toi last term, but Soldier Reeves (3-1) was the stronger at the finish and passed the post with three and a quarter lengths in hand.
- Coral Gold Cup best bets from the Sky Sports Racing team
- Three for the Coral Gold Cup! Sean Boyce's Newbury preview
Skelton will now point his emerging stayer to Ascot's Long Walk Hurdle just before Christmas.
He said: "I was very impressed with him and I wasn't surprised he won, but I was surprised he could do it first time out.
"He still didn't relax all that well, but he relaxed well enough for Harry to be able to get him switched off and he came home strongly.
"I didn't go to three miles in the spring and this makes me glad I didn't. We may have left a big race behind not going three miles at Aintree, but I just knew if I did that when he was just a five-year-old I might have been asking too much. I trusted him today and he delivered."
He went on: "He was under the radar, but that's because he wasn't quite behaving well enough to win one of those last year.
"I put that down to the fact he was very raw at four and five. We only went hurdling last year because I was so annoyed with him for pulling so hard in a bumper at Newton Abbot that I sent him hurdling to try to slow him down with a few jumps in front of him.
"He has just improved and improved and improved and he has a brilliant engine. He had some good rivals around him at the last and I was very impressed he could come out on top as I thought it was a very competitive renewal.
"I have a lot of respect for the horses he has beaten there and now he will have to try to back it up. The one thing about this horse though is he has a fantastic attitude and we'll go now to the Long Walk."
Race regular Strong Leader could renew rivalry at Ascot, although Olly Murphy will also consider a trip to Ireland.
Murphy said: "He ran well but just bumped into a younger, better horse on the day. We have no excuse whatsoever and although people love to knock this horse and he's not always great at Cheltenham, nine times out of 10 he turns up and runs a great race.
"He always jumps the last looking like the winner, but today he has bumped into a better one and we'll dust ourselves down and go again.
"Whether we go Ascot at Christmas or Ireland, I'm not sure, but there is still life in him yet. He loves a left-handed flat track and yes he ran very well in a Long Walk last year, but Ireland is certainly something we'll have a good look at.
"We'll see how he comes out of today and he's run a cracker and I'm really proud of him. He deserves to win a big one again, but it's life and sometimes you bump into a nice young horse who is just too good on the day."
Taurus Bay emulates The Jukebox Man
Taurus Bay followed in the hoofprints of illustrious stablemate The Jukebox Man by winning the Coral John Francome Novices' Chase.
It is two years since Harry Redknapp's subsequent King George hero made a winning debut over fences in this Grade Two contest and in his younger stablemate the popular owner, trainer Ben Pauling and jockey Ben Jones appear to have unearthed another potential star.
Taurus Bay lined up having already won over the larger obstacles in the Rising Stars Novices' Chase at Aintree three weeks ago, a victory which meant the 11-8 favourite had to concede 3lb to each of his four rivals in his bid for back-to-back Group Two wins.
Harry Skelton ensured the race was a stern test of stamina and jumping aboard the front-running Royal Infantry, but Jones steadily nursed Taurus Bay into contention and he toughed it out on the run-in to prevail by half a length.
Pauling said: "It's lovely to work with horses who try as hard as that when they need to. He didn't have the run of the race and was in a tight pocket and Ben was patient when he needed to be today, which was great.
"We all know the Skelton team are going to be very hard to pass and are never here to make up the numbers, but I was always confident jumping two out and after the last he was going to tough it out.
"Ben would have liked him to have travelled a little bit better early doors, but that might have been because the ground was a little lively for him. I would love to get some soft ground for this horse soon because that's when we'll see him at his best.
"We definitely won't be going up in trip and I would come back in trip before I go up. I even think two miles on soft ground could be where he's at his best.

items.title: Haaland ‘happy’ at Man City despite outburst that led to transfer talk
items.summary:
Haaland ‘happy’ at Man City despite outburst that led to transfer talk
Erling Haaland blasted beleaguered City’s form, but ahead of Arsenal test, manager Enzo Maresca says striker is happy.
Enzo Maresca insisted on Friday that Erling Haaland is “happy” at Manchester City after the striker expressed
items.text:
Haaland ‘happy’ at Man City despite outburst that led to transfer talk
Erling Haaland blasted beleaguered City’s form, but ahead of Arsenal test, manager Enzo Maresca says striker is happy.
Enzo Maresca insisted on Friday that Erling Haaland is “happy” at Manchester City after the striker expressed frustration over his side’s recent struggles.
Haaland gave a candid assessment of City’s malaise following Tuesday’s 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League, which came on the back of a Premier League draw at home with Fulham.
After winning 10 of their first 11 matches in all competitions this season, Maresca’s men have won just two of their last seven.
With a crucial trip to Premier League leaders Arsenal looming on Sunday, Haaland’s criticism added to the growing sense that City’s season is in danger of spiralling out of control.
“We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way,” Haaland said.
“I have no idea what we were missing but you could feel it in the last few games that something was not clicking fully.”
Haaland has scored just once in his last five games for City and is without a league goal in his past three matches.
The Norway star’s body language has been noticeably angst-ridden in recent weeks, prompting suggestions that he is growing disillusioned with life at the Etihad Stadium.
City are also awaiting the result of their appeal against a guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, with the punishment potentially including a huge points deduction.
Despite City’s woes, Maresca is adamant Haaland remains committed to the cause regardless of speculation that he could seek a move at the end of the season.
“Erling is a nine; they live for goals and winning games. If they don’t score, they are upset. I think he gesticulates in the same way when we are winning games,” Maresca told reporters on Friday.
“For sure he is not happy because we are not winning games. But it is not just Erling. Everyone is on the same page.
“He has been good. He has been normal since day one. Two or three weeks ago, he was dancing inside the pitch and in the training sessions.
“He is happy. It is normal that results affect the mood a little bit but I don’t see any problem with Erling. He is a winner.”
Maresca will need Haaland back to his best against Arsenal if third-placed City are to earn a vital victory over the champions.
Already trailing six points behind Arsenal, a defeat in north London would be a huge blow to their title hopes.
Maresca has come under fire during City’s slump in his first season after replacing Pep Guardiola.
The former Chelsea boss claimed teething problems were inevitable during the transition from Guardiola’s dynastic reign.
“Transition requires time. It’s probably because we won seven games in a row, everyone was thinking at City there’s no transition,” Maresca said.
“But I’ve said many times I’m not a magician. There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new.
“For sure, when you don’t win games, it’s not the ideal situation. For me, it’s completely normal, I’m completely relaxed, no panic at all.”

items.title: Maresca: You can't compare Man City and Arsenal
items.summary:
Arsenal vs Man City: Enzo Maresca says two teams cannot be compared due to being in different stages of project
Arsenal and Man City face off in the Premier League this weekend with the Gunners holding a six-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side; Mikel Arteta says the game is important for the title f
items.text:
Arsenal vs Man City: Enzo Maresca says two teams cannot be compared due to being in different stages of project
Arsenal and Man City face off in the Premier League this weekend with the Gunners holding a six-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side; Mikel Arteta says the game is important for the title fight; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
Friday 27 November 2026 15:33, UK
Enzo Maresca said Premier League title rivals Manchester City and Arsenal couldn’t be compared after his side's early-season form raised expectations.
Maresca described Sunday's fixture, live on Sky Sports, as "four months vs seven years", referencing the transition City are going through following Pep Guardiola's departure and the longevity of head coach Mikel Arteta at Arsenal.
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
"We have been top of the league for two and a half months until November 1. Now we are not there and everyone is comparing," said Maresca.
"For me, it's seven years together against four months together so you cannot compare. I understand everyone is trying to do that, but from my point of view everything is clear."
City have fallen six points behind Arsenal after failing to win in their last four league games while they've only won two of their last seven in all competitions.
"It's more than easy to understand why because we've had four months together," said Maresca when addressing his side's form.
"Transition requires time. Probably because we won seven games in a row, eight with the Champions League, everyone was thinking that there was no transition.
"I said many times, I'm not a magician. There's a transition, it's normal. We have eight or nine new players, the manager is new, so you need time.
"You can see with different clubs when they transition, how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal.
"I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all, understanding that we need to win games because it's our business. For me, it's all normal."
'No issue with Haaland after midweek comments'
In midweek, Erling Haaland made some concerning comments, claiming that "you have to question everything" after their draw against Napoli in the Champions League. But Maresca insists there is no issue with the striker.
"It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games," said Maresca. "I don't see any problem with Erling."
"Erling is a winner. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games. Not just Erling, everyone. Don't forget, three weeks ago, he was dancing on the pitch."
Maresca is prioritising the long-term vision he has for City. "The present is important but the future is much more important in terms of improving and building something with the team.
"Where we can be on Sunday night if we win, lose or draw, it's important but it's a long season. We'll see where we are in February and March and from there you can set the goals.
"Now, I think it's useless speaking about targets or where we can be at the end of the season."
But facing champions Arsenal on Sunday will give them idea of their progress.
"You need to show personality," he said. "That's why it's also a nice game for us to see where we are in terms of personality and from there try to understand the situation."
Arteta: These games are important for the title
In the red corner, Arsenal manager Arteta knows how important matches are against their rivals in their bid to retain the Premier League title for the first time.
"When we played the home games against big teams, that becomes crucial in the title challenge," he said. "We know how important the home games are to make the difference.
"But we're in November, we know how long we have to play. But that's for every single team."
Asked whether City's form has anything to do with the club being found guilty of 115 serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in September, Arteta admitted that "it's a question for City."
He then went on to say: "All I can say is when I watch them play is a lot of games that they have done more merits than the opponent, but this is football. To win games, that's merit to the way they play."
Asked if City are Arsenal's closest challengers for the title, Arteta replied: "We don't know, I think the challenge is for us, and the opportunity is for us.
"We cannot control what the opponents are going to do; we just need to give ourselves the best version, and I'm sure the atmosphere is going to be incredible on Sunday, and we need to enjoy and embrace those kinds of games and go for it."
Arteta did not, however, want to be drawn on the atmosphere the Emirates Stadium could produce in the wake of City's guilty verdict. The club deny all the charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict. No sanctions have yet been announced.
On the pitch, Arsenal are sweating on the fitness of goalkeeper David Raya while centre-back William Saliba will have to wait patiently to work his way back into the side following injury.
For City, the game comes too soon for winger Antoine Semenyo, who could return next week.

items.title: 'I am not a magician' - what can Maresca's Man City learn from watertight Arsenal?
items.summary:
'I am not a magician' - what can Maresca's Man City learn from watertight Arsenal?
- Published
Manchester City's leaky defence faces one of its most difficult tasks of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal, aiming to put right their patchy recent form.
Enzo Maresca's side began the season wit
items.text:
'I am not a magician' - what can Maresca's Man City learn from watertight Arsenal?
- Published
Manchester City's leaky defence faces one of its most difficult tasks of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal, aiming to put right their patchy recent form.
Enzo Maresca's side began the season with eight straight victories but have won only one of their past seven in all competitions inside 90 minutes and head to Emirates Stadium trailing the champions by six points even at this early juncture.
A Premier League defeat on Sunday could well have long-term consequences for City's title aspirations, with Mikel Arteta's men clearly standing above any other top-flight side as the ones to topple.
Though the Gunners dropped points last weekend with a draw at Newcastle, they continue to set the standards with a miserly defence that has conceded only seven goals in the club's opening 11 league games.
Asked why he felt City have dropped off in recent weeks, Maresca - who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager in the summer - said: "For me it's because we've had four months together. Transition requires time.
"It's probably because we won seven games in a row, with Champions League eight in a row. Everyone was thinking at City there's no transition but I've said many times I am not a magician. There is transition, it's normal.
"There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new so you need time and you can see different clubs when they had transition how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all."
- 'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt 
  - Published2 days ago
- Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League 
  - Published2 days ago
Clean sheets gone missing
"We are conceding too many goals and we need to avoid that," was an obvious statement made by Maresca following last Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.
City followed that up with another home stalemate against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday and have now conceded in 10 successive games in all competitions for the first time in seven years.
"[It was] far, far too easy to play through [City]," said former England captain Alan Shearer of Rodrigo Muniz's goal for Fulham on Match of the Day.
"Fulham's throw-in was level with their own 18-yard box. For them to get through is not acceptable at any level, let alone when you are playing for Manchester City and Muniz ran past the entire midfield [to score]."
City have managed only five clean sheets all campaign, which is in stark contrast to Arsenal, who have kept double the amount so far, while Newcastle's opening goal ended a run off 445 minutes without the ball hitting their net.
Maresca's men also have an issue by conceding the opener, having done so seven times in the past 10 games, and of the 14 goals they have shipped, six have come inside the first 20 minutes.
An early Arsenal goal may well be an important factor in deciding Sunday's contest.
Asked how his side can improve defensively, Maresca said: "Video [analysis], meetings, [on] pitch coaching, It is a mix of that.
"Some of the goals we concede we can avoid, so hopefully we can do that."
Lack of continuity leading to errors?
The injury to key defender William Saliba has almost gone unnoticed for Arsenal as Ezri Konsa has stepped in to fill the void at centre-back seamlessly since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.
The England international has established a formidable partnership with Gabriel and the two have quickly formed an impressive understanding this season.
Maresca, meanwhile, admitted he was still "trying to find different" solutions to his team, which has been highlighted by the chopping and changing of his backline.
In 16 Premier League and Champions League games this season, the Italian has used eight different combinations in defence, which has given players little chance of fostering any sort of on-pitch relationships with each other.
City have also made seven errors leading to goals, compared to Arsenal's one.
"You are concerned in some way because that is a lot of errors leading to goals," said former City defender Nedum Onuoha. "With some of the best players you ask, 'what are they really good at?' For some it is the fact they don't make mistakes.
"They are ruthless and relentless in the way they play but at this moment in time City are being punished for those errors.
"A manager can have the tactics and do the team talks, but if people are going to continue to make those mistakes, they will suffer."
Edging victories
The chant of "1-0 to the Arsenal" has been synonymous with the Gunners over the years and it could not be more apt under Arteta.
Since the start of last season, his side have won 16 matches in all competitions by that particular scoreline, compared to six by City.
After beating Sunderland in a chaotic match in September, Maresca said he would "prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3", suggesting his side needed more control and he re-iterated that message after the Fulham draw.
"Sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference and to keep a clean sheet but in this moment we are not able to do that," he admitted.
City, though, have scored five more league goals than Arsenal in this campaign and Sunday's hosts have injury concerns over goalkeeper David Raya.
The Spaniard is a doubt with the shoulder problem he picked up at Newcastle, and compatriot Kepa Arrizabalaga may deputise again as he did in the 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.
City have fond memories of coming up against Arsenal's stand-in keeper, after Kepa's howler for the opening goal contributed to their 2-0 Carabao Cup final triumph back in March.
A repeat result on Sunday will provide a much-needed morale boost for Maresca and his team.

Kimi Antonelli dominated first practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as he led team-mate George Russell in a Mercedes one-two.
New Formula 1 world champion Antonelli was half a second faster than Russell and 0.661s quicker than Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, who was the fastest non-Mercedes in third.

Georgian police said 16 people were detained and three officers "sustained
items.text:
Georgia: Police clash with Besiktas fans at Israel club game
November 27, 2026
A football game between a Turkish and an Israeli team in Georgia's Batumi was disrupted by violence, with UEFA due to assess the events on Friday.
Georgian police said 16 people were detained and three officers "sustained various injuries as a result of the fans' violent actions" during the match.
The police also accused some supporters of hurling stadium seats at security forces.
Turkey's Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva were originally set to meet in Istanbul, but with the tensions between the two countries running high due to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, UEFA decided to move the match to Georgia for safety reasons.
Georgia denies police were deployed over Palestine support
During the Thursday game, Besiktas fans unfurled a banner, "Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine," waved Palestinian flags and chanted anti-Israel slogans.
However, Georgian authorities insisted they did not intervene due to the fans expressing their support for the Palestinians.
"We categorically deny these reports and emphasize that the fans' violent actions and physical clashes with police began before the flags and banners were displayed, while they were still marching towards the stadium," said the Georgian Interior Ministry.
In turn, Besiktas accused the authorities of using "disproportionate force" against the fans, and Turkey's football federation condemned "the unacceptable attitudes, behavior and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium."
A Besiktas club employee told the AFP news agency that five Turkish fans were taken to a hospital for medical treatment.
The match was suspended for over half an hour due to the violence in the stands. Eventually, Danish referee Morten Krogh continued the game, which ended with Besiktas winning 2 to 1.
The Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency reported.
Turkish government ministers close ranks with Besiktas
The unrest has prompted a diplomatic incident between Turkey and Georgia.
Turkish sources indicated Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan discussed the clashes with his Georgian counterpart Maka Botchorishvili.
Meanwhile, Turkish Sports Minister Osman Askin Bak and Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci echoed Besiktas' accusations of "disproportionate" force used by the Georgian police.
In an online post, Bak pledged to continue "resolutely defend the rights of Turkish sport and our fans."
Turkish news agency IHA reported that the 16 detained Besiktas fans have been released due to diplomatic and legal steps ordered by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
According to Besiktas, Erdogan also spoke to the club chairman, telling the sports official he was closely monitoring the situation.

items.text:
Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy amid rising fuel costs
November 27, 2026
Norwegian low-cost, long-haul airline Norse Atlantic's operating unit has declared bankruptcy, the carrier said on Friday.
The airline had warned on Wednesday that its financial situation was "critical," and suspended all flights the following day, saying it was urgently seeking emergency funding to fend off bankruptcy.
Like many commercial airlines, Norse Atlantic is highly exposed to the vastly increased jet fuel prices of 2026, attributable in very large part to the war in Iran and resultant tension throughout the wider Middle East.
What did Norse Atlantic say about the bankruptcy filing?
Norse had said slightly earlier on Friday that its lessors had terminated their leasing contracts for all 12 aircraft in the carrier's fleet, demanding that the planes be handed back. Initially the company said it planned to contest this claim, which would have rendered it effectively unable to operate.
But the announcement of plans to file for bankruptcy followed fairly soon after.
"The Board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the company and the group to find a solution," Norse CEO Eivind Roald said in a statement.
Other companies in the group like the stock market-listed Norse Atlantic ASA parent company and the Norse Atlantic UK subsidiary are not part of the filing and are still attempting to stay in business, the company said.
"The board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations," Roald said.
The company said on Thursday that it planned to file for bankruptcy unless financing could be arranged and had warned: "There can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found."
Founded just five years ago and based in Arendal in Norway, Norse Atlantic had a fleet of 12 planes and serviced a total of 14 destinations. It had recorded a net loss of $61.9 million (€56.5 million) in 2025, even before the additional economic strains caused by the war in Iran.
Why has the war in Iran put such strain on the aviation industry?
Small and lower-cost airlines are struggling in particular, but the aviation industry in general is facing severe problems amid the strains on global fuel deliveries caused by the conflict in the Gulf.
In early 2026, as the US launched attacks on Iran — soon leading to reduced traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — aviation fuel rapidly spiked, more than doubling in price at its peak.
It rose higher even than in the immediate aftermath of Russia's full scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Although it dipped in mid-summer amid hopes of a resolution to the conflict, it rose once again as these faded and a stalemate developed.
This has posed the worst crisis for the industry since the COVID pandemic drastically reduced the volume of air traffic in 2020 and beyond, a much larger issue that many carriers were still struggling to recover from.
