Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport.
This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) Davi
items.text:
Man City owners should be forced to sell, say rival club chiefs
- Published
Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport.
This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) David Kogan claimed he has the "stomach" to take action against City, who deny wrongdoing and have appealed.
The IFR has the power to remove directors of a club if they are deemed unsuitable, and even force a sale in the most serious cases.
Now, executives at three top-flight rivals have told the BBC that they believe this is the appropriate punishment for City, who were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations rules between 2009 and 2018, and failing to co-operate with an investigation.
- Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue 
  - Published19 November
- Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City 
  - Published6 October
The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league.
But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy.
In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by some of City's rivals, another claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by £900m through "sham" commercial arrangements.
Manchester City's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour.
The executive who spoke anonymously said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment.
Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September.
But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established.
It also comes amid mounting questions over whether wider UAE trade and investment in UK projects could be impacted by such a move. In September, Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to City's owners selling the club, adding that "they have been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester".
When approached, the IFR declined to comment. But Kogan has consistently said that the IFR will not be influenced by any political pressure.
Earlier this week he told a parliamentary committee that the watchdog would not be afraid to investigate City's hierarchy and take action, depending on the outcome of the appeal.
"Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue. We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size," Kogan said.
"We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that's been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.
"But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so... assuming those circumstances are triggered, if we don't act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?"
When asked how any potential legal battles with Manchester City would be paid for, IFR chief executive Richard Monks told MPs that a litigation reserve of £2m was to be built up over the next two years via the levy charged to clubs, which would be paid back if litigation was successful.
"Now clearly - and I'm not talking about a specific case - clearly, there could be a very large legal case of any particular club that would require us to spend more than £2m in terms of litigation costs and barrister costs in particular", Monks added. "So if that happens, we have agreed with government [that it] will effectively lend us the money in terms of cash flow.
"We'd expect to win that litigation, to claim costs and repay government. If we failed in that massive litigation, then ultimately it would be added to the levy and we'd repay government that way."
Last month it was revealed that the IFR would cost clubs in the top five divisions of English men's football £20.3m annually.
Last week, Premier League clubs voted to cover legal expenses for its five board directors if any of City's sponsors sued them. Two UAE-based commercial partners - Etihad and Etisalat - have both said they are considering legal action against the Premier League.
The IFR has the authority to force a sale within section 34 of the Football Governance Act which allows it to investigate whether an owner meets the required suitability standards around honest, integrity and financial soundness. If an owner fails this assessment, the regulator can direct them to take reasonable steps to relinquish ownership within a specified period before issuing an ownership removal order.

items.summary:
Buffalo Bills 13-10 Kansas City Chiefs: Tyler Bass hits 57-yard field goal in final seconds to snatch victory over NFL rivals
Buffalo Bills beat rivals Kansas City Chiefs thanks to a 57-yard field goal from Tyler Bass; he also hit a 54-yard field goal to level the game with 12 minutes remaining
Frid
items.text:
Buffalo Bills 13-10 Kansas City Chiefs: Tyler Bass hits 57-yard field goal in final seconds to snatch victory over NFL rivals
Buffalo Bills beat rivals Kansas City Chiefs thanks to a 57-yard field goal from Tyler Bass; he also hit a 54-yard field goal to level the game with 12 minutes remaining
Friday 27 November 2026 06:29, UK
Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal on the hooter as Buffalo Bills improved their AFC-leading record to 10-1 with a 13-10 victory over rivals Kansas City Chiefs.
James Cook had 117 yards rushing and scored on a five-yard run and Bass also made a 54-yard field goal in the defensive struggle.
The highly anticipated fireworks between Buffalo's Josh Allen and Kansas City's Patrick Mahomes, two of the NFL's best quarterbacks, and top offenses failed to materialise.
- How to watch NFL Thanksgiving week live on Sky Sports
- Jay-Z picks himself to headline Super Bowl half-time show
- Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW
Allen finished 10 of 21 for 81 yards with two interceptions - both coming inside the Kansas City 20. Mahomes finished 16 of 29 for 174 yards.
Buffalo have won seven straight and matched their best start to a season since 1991.
Emmett Johnson had 72 yards rushing and scored on a one-yard run for the Chiefs.
Neither offense could muster much momentum with rain falling through the evening and cold gusts that made it feel like -5.
Bass's decisive kick came after the Chiefs went three-and-out at their own 11 with 15 seconds remaining. Matt Araiza's punt was partially tipped by Joe Andreessen, leading to a line-drive ball fielded by Greg Dortch, who returned it 17 yards to Kansas City's 39 with four seconds remaining.
Bass's 54-yard field goal to tie it at 10 some 12 minutes earlier also was struck in the same direction.
Kansas City's Harrison Butker, kicking in the other direction toward the north end of the stadium, missed a go-ahead 46-yard attempt wide right with just over five minutes remaining.
In their seventh regular-season meeting since 2020, the Bills improved to 6-1, including six straight wins over Kansas City. The Chiefs, however, hold a 4-0 edge in the playoffs, including two AFC championship game wins.
After Cook opened the scoring 28 seconds into the second quarter, Allen squandered a chance to build a 14-0 lead on the Bills next possession. Facing second-and-eight at the Chiefs nine, Allen rolled to his right, appeared to have his pass slightly tipped by George Karlaftis, and intercepted by Alohi Gilman in the end zone.
It marked the first time in 43 drives inside an opponent's 20 the Bills failed to come away with points this season.
He would turn it over again in the red zone two drives later on Buffalo's first possession of the second half. On first-and-10 at Kansas City's 14, Allen's sidearm pass to Khalil Shakir was low, glanced off the receiver's hands and deflected into the arms of Nohl Williams.
Allen has five touchdowns versus seven interceptions in his past five starts.
The Chiefs continue to face questions over whether they have padded their record with weaker opponents. Of their eight wins, only one - a season-opening victory against Denver - has come against an opponent with a winning record entering Week 12. Meantime, all three losses have come against winning teams.
The Bills, meanwhile, were coming off a four-game stretch in which they feasted in playing against backup and third-string quarterbacks.
Buffalo limited the NFL's best offense to 241 yards and contained Mahomes, who entered the outing combined for 13 TDs passing and averaging 309 yards over his past four games.
Buffalo did allow their first touchdown in four outings, dating to to Derrick Henry's two-yard run in a 36-10 win over Baltimore on November 1. They were also limited to a season-low 230 yards.

items.text:
Photograph by Rachel Claire
Latest updates from Buy Nothing Day on FACEBOOK
Buy Nothing Day takes place on Friday November 27th, it's a 24 hour detox from consumerism and an opportunity for you to tune into the impact we have on the environment through shopping.
People around the world will make a pact with themselves to take a break from consumption as a personal experiment or public statement, and the best thing is - IT'S FREE!!!
                  
Photograph by Mumtahina Tanni
Photograph by Kris Hsieh
 Buy Nothing Day was started by Adbusters in the early 90's and has since grown into an international event celebrated in more the 50 countries. Its is a simple idea, which challenges consumer culture by asking us to switch off from shopping for a day. The day is celebrated as a holiday by some, a street party by others - anyone can take part provided they spend a day without spending!
The UK campaign and website was created in 2000 by Michael Smith a graphic designer who cares passionately about environmental and ethical issues. The message has always been simple, ‘Shop Less, Live More’. Twenty one years on - the message couldn't be any simpler - WE NEED TO CONSUME LESS! Recycling is good - reducing is better!
There are serious issues linked to shopping, which expose the environmental and ethical consequences of consumerism. The rich western countries - only 20% of the world population are consuming over 80% of the earth's natural resources, causing a disproportionate level of environmental damage and unfair distribution of wealth.
As consumers we need to question our culture of shopping. We all have different needs and ultimately we are all consumers and will never be able to escape culture altogether. But this shouldn’t stop us from questioning the products we buy or challenging the companies, who produce them. After all, what are the true risk consumerism poses to the environment and developing countries? The arguments are infinite - but there is no reason why we shouldn’t be looking for simple solutions now because one day we may be forced to change.
The issues connected with Buy Nothing Day are broad and deep, however, the campaign focuses on promoting ethical and responsible consumerism, recycling, re-using and ultimately cutting back on what we consume - its a big challenge!
People have become aware that large corporations are exploiting labour conditions in developing countries using up vital resources because they are cheap and there aren't the systems to protect workers or the environment like there are in the west. The gap between the rich and poor nations is growing in spite of the much-heralded benefits of globalisation, there are still 1.3 billion people world wide who live on less than $3 a day and a similar number of people do not have access to clean water.
Workers rights in developing countries are frequently violated, including payment of low wages and long working hours. The lives of workers may also be endangered by poor health and safety provision. Child labour is rife in developing countries, and forced labour still exists. Unfortunately most people don't think of these things while shopping.
Supporters of globalisation offer economic growth as a solution to world poverty. They propose that impoverished nations and individuals can eventually attain a standard of living similar to our own through the 'trickle down' of wealth. However, the current globalisation model is leading to an increase in world poverty and inequality. 
Buy Nothing Day is non-confrontational, it’s not a protest. All we ask people to do is switch off from shopping, have a bit of fun, use their imagination and simply escape consumerism for a day. If people laugh at the ingenuity and genius of Buy Nothing Day, then we’ve got their attention and we're opening the door to change.

items.text:
For years now, I’ve made it an annual tradition to replace one or two hard drives on Black Friday. I typically run around ten physical disks, and swapping a couple out each year means I almost never have a drive older than five years in my systems. I’ve even previously made videos about shucking disks around this time of year.
But current hardware pricing is totally screwed. So what is a lifelong self-hoster to do in times like these? With disk capacities increasing massively over the last 10 years I can now fit 20TB per slot. This means I could realistically go from ten spinners to five, and not really feel it too acutely. This will mean redoing my zpool layouts, which in turn means shuffling some data around as ZFS doesn’t like changes to the layout of existing pools. But, at these prices, I’m starting to think the hassle might be worth it.
Let’s take a look at disk prices over the past 8 years in today’s post.
The 20TB WD EasyStore I bought for $249.99 in November 2024 is, today, on sale, $549.99 this Black Friday. $300 more than 2 years ago for the same product, from the same store. It shows just how bad hard drive pricing has gotten (BestBuy 20TB listing).
Shucking is homelab speak for taking a perfectly good external drive out of its USB enclosure and sticking the SATA drive in your server. At $12.50/TB it was a fantastically affordable way to get massive amounts of storage. At $27.50/TB, absolutely not.
I dug through my receipts
In November 2018 I bought five 10TB EasyStores for $179.99 each. At the time I wrote about doing the rounds of my local Best Buys to pickup more drives on Black Friday as quantities were limited at each location (My 2018 server build log).
October 2023 was my best haul on a per-TB basis. Three 18TB drives put 54TB in my hands for $599.97. This year’s “deal” is fifty bucks shy of that entire order. Best Buy was still advertising those 18TB drives for $199.99 in November 2023. November 2023 deal archive
What about ServerPartDeals?
Buying refurbished or recertified enterprise drives used to be an easy way to bring the cost down. In August 2024 I bought four recertified 14TB Ultrastars from ServerPartDeals for $529.96 before tax. That was 56TB at $9.46/TB, even cheaper than the EasyStores and no shucking to do.
The sad truth is that across the board prices are up a minimum of 58%, and sometimes as much as 218% in just a year or two.
How we got down to three HDD makers
When the EasyStore is that bad, my first instinct is to shop around. Maybe I should try another retailer (to be clear I’m not blaming BestBuy for any of this), buy an enterprise drive, see what’s available recertified. But follow those listings back to the companies that actually make the drives and the choices narrow pretty quickly. There are three big HDD makers left. How did we end up with so few?
Maxtor bought Quantum’s hard drive business in 2001, then Seagate bought Maxtor in 2006. Hitachi combined IBM’s disk business with its own to form HGST in 2003, and Toshiba bought Fujitsu’s HDD business in 2009. Seagate bought Samsung’s HDD business in December 2011, and Western Digital bought HGST in March 2012. The FTC required WD to sell desktop-drive manufacturing assets to Toshiba to keep a third supplier in that market. That left Seagate, Western Digital and Toshiba.
The 2011 Thailand floods hit while those last two deals were underway. WD halted production at all its Thai plants, and its average hard drive selling price went from $45 in fiscal 2011 to $62 in fiscal 2012. There was also a price-fixing case further up the supply chain. NHK Spring pleaded guilty in 2019 to fixing prices for the suspension assemblies that hold the read/write heads, and the court approved a $28.5 million fine. WD’s 2012 annual report · Ninth Circuit opinion
Market collusion and cartel pricing
It’s hard to have anything positive to say in this post. The HDD manufacturing market is so consolidated nowadays - just like the memory market which is equally screwed - that it’s hard to see this as anything but mass market collusion by the HDD manufacturing cartel.
Three companies is an awfully short list when you need to buy a hard drive. And with 89% of WD’s revenue coming from its cloud business in fiscal 2026, I don’t reckon those of us buying a couple of drives for a home server have much impact here. Just like with Nvidia and Micron, consumer markets just aren’t valuable enough so we have to make do with the crumbs instead.
As of November 26, 2026, the 20TB is 2.2× what I paid for the exact same SKU in 2024. It’s also $270 more than I paid for it in May 2025. And if you’re thinking you’ll just buy a smaller one, Best Buy’s 8TB Black Friday special is $299.99. That’s $37.50/TB and fifty bucks more than my 20TB cost two years ago. Best Buy’s EasyStore listings
The jump gets sillier when you price a whole NAS. Four of those 20TB drives would have been $999.96 at my 2024 price. This week they’d be $2,199.96. That’s another $1,200 before you’ve bought a case, a board or a single stick of RAM. And the price per usable terabyte only gets worse once you set aside a drive for parity.
If I can wish for one thing in 2027, it would be for hardware pricing to return to reasonable levels. I fear it may take a lot longer than that, though. So making do with less is going to be the new normal for a while. And in that creative constraint, maybe we’ll have some fun along the way instead.

items.title: Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly convicted over attack on UK couple
items.summary:
Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly convicted over attack on UK couple
- Published
A Kenyan woodcutter who was wrongly convicted and sentenced to death over an attack on a British couple has told the BBC that actions by London's Metropolitan Police involved in the case destroyed his l
items.text:
Met Police ruined my life, says Kenyan man wrongly convicted over attack on UK couple
- Published
A Kenyan woodcutter who was wrongly convicted and sentenced to death over an attack on a British couple has told the BBC that actions by London's Metropolitan Police involved in the case destroyed his life.
Somali gunmen broke into David and Judith Tebbutt's beach bungalow on the Kenyan coast in 2011. They shot David dead and abducted Judith, holding her captive in Somalia for six months.
Met detectives flew to Kenya to assist the investigation. Their evidence helped convict Ali Kololo, who spent more than a decade in prison before his conviction was overturned.
Kololo is suing the Met, claiming a senior officer, former Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd, gave misleading evidence at his trial and acted unlawfully to secure his conviction.
In his first media interview, he told the BBC about his 15-year ordeal and his fight for compensation, which the Met is challenging in court.
We meet on Lamu, a small island off Kenya's northern coast, once a thriving Swahili port. People and goods are still carted through its narrow stone streets by donkey rather than car.
It was here, in 2013, that Kololo was sentenced to death.
Standing at the jetty, where police once brought him ashore in handcuffs, he relishes being free. But he is struggling to rebuild his life.
"Everything was taken from me. I'm starting from zero. I don't think I'll ever go back to who I was before," he says.
Before his arrest, Kololo lived with his wife and their three young children. He had once worked as a groundskeeper at the resort where the Tebbutts were staying, but by 2011 he earned his living felling trees in a local forest and selling the wood.
"My life was very good," he says. "I was fending for myself, taking good care of my family."
Within 24 hours of the attack, Kenyan police had arrested him.
"I was beaten with clubs and thrown into a car," he says. "They beat me for days, burning me with cigarettes, forcing me to confess to things. They subjected me to torture like no other."
Kololo could not read or write. He says police made him put his thumbprint on a statement claiming he had led the attackers to the Tebbutts.
"I didn't understand anything," he says, calling the statement "a mountain of lies". "I signed it without knowing what it was because of the state they had put me in".
The Kenyan police told us it "at all times strives to work within the law". Kololo is not suing them.
Within days of the attack, a team of Met officers, led by then Detective Superintendent Neil Hibberd, arrived to support the Kenyan investigation. The UK government had instructed the officers not to accept information from the Kenyan authorities that had been obtained by interrogating detainees.
But Hibberd requested Kololo's statement and later relied on it when giving evidence for the prosecution at his trial.
In court, Hibberd also presented evidence linking Kololo to the attack. He told the Kenyan court Kololo had been wearing a type of shoe that matched footwear marks found in the sand at the resort.
The officer who had arrested Kololo said he was barefoot when he was handed to police. Hibberd did not disclose that the Met's own forensic examination could not establish whether the shoe in question had made the marks.
At the trial, Kololo did not initially have a lawyer. He had to cross-examine all the prosecution witnesses himself, including Hibberd, through an interpreter who spoke Swahili, which was not Kololo's first language.
"I believe I was framed because I am a poor man and I did not have the strength or means to fight for myself," Kololo says.
Kololo was convicted of kidnap and robbery with violence - the only person ever convicted in connection with the attack. He spent three years on death row before his sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.
He recalls seeing his prison file. In the space for the expiry date, someone had written "death".
"I was completely heartbroken. I believed I could be executed at any moment, and I would never see my family, my children, ever again."
Years later, the UK's Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) established that Hibberd had omitted significant forensic evidence at the trial. It found that he would have had a case to answer for gross misconduct, but he could not face disciplinary proceedings because he had retired from the force. At the time, his lawyer said Hibberd absolutely disagreed with the report's findings.
In April 2023, Kenya's High Court quashed Kololo's conviction, because of doubts over the prosecution's evidence. This followed years of work by the legal charity Reprieve and a Kenyan lawyer, Alfred Olaba, who represented him for free.
They were supported by Judith Tebbutt, who believed Kololo was innocent. In an interview with the BBC in 2022, she said he had been scapegoated by Scotland Yard.
"He was not there on the night. He was not part of the group that held me. They've put this man in prison without any real evidence."
More than three years after his release, Kololo says he is still living with the effects of his torture and decade in prison. As we walk the narrow streets of Lamu's old town, his thin frame moves stiffly. He is on edge. "My mind is not good," he says. "I have not recovered."
He remembers being kept in a filthy, bedbug-ridden cell with up to eight other inmates, which he thought he would never leave. Twice he contracted tuberculosis and nearly died.
Kololo is now too frail to do the woodcutting he once relied on to make a living. He tries to grow enough to eat on the land around his home, but erratic rain makes it difficult.
"I have nothing. On the days I get food, I eat, and on the days I don't, I endure."
He lives alone in a mud hut. His wife divorced him after he went to prison, and their children went to live with his mother. They dropped out of school because the family could not pay the fees. Kololo says they were not allowed to visit him

items.text:
'Priceless' Duran proves 'the man' but is he papering over cracks at Celtic?
- Published
"Duran is priceless for us at the moment".
It would be difficult for a football manager to muster up a higher compliment for one of his players - given he should know exactly how much he did cost - but Celtic boss Martin O'Neill was rightly effusive in his praise for Camilo Duran.
With 15 goals in 23 appearances, six assists, and another late European winner on Thursday, the Colombian was once again the main man for a struggling Celtic side.
His double against Besiktas breathed life into their Europa League campaign last time out, and his late leap to nod in the winner against Torreense kept it alive.
Duran, 24, started on the bench but was brought on with just over half an hour to go as O'Neill watched his side labour against a team currently 13th in the Portuguese second tier.
Celtic would still be searching for their first European win were it not for their summer arrival from Qarabag, whose goals have played a key part in keeping his team within touching distance of a play-off spot with three fixtures to play.
"He's taken on this mantle of being the man and he's been fantastic," said O'Neill, who started Duran on the bench. "We tried a similar approach against Besiktas.
"Sometimes by the time Duran gets subbed on, you could be behind. But I think that's the sign of a brilliant player, he'll do something.
"He's not a big guy but he's just a super footballer, a super, super footballer."
Papering over cracks or quality in depth?
Duran's summer arrival was overshadowed when, just over a fortnight later, a club-record fee was paid to Bodo Glimt for another striker, Kasper Hogh.
While recent weeks have been dominated by debates over Duran or Hogh, the debate now seems settled, with the Colombian operating on a different level from his striking counterpart.
Anyone watching Celtic in Portugal would have watched Hogh find space a handful of times in the area, but repeatedly fail to find a team-mate or trouble the goalkeeper. Duran didn't need to be asked twice.
"I don't know how many touches he got, but he had the telling touch," James McFadden said on Sportsound post-match.
Duran's goals have also proved decisive in securing domestic points against Falkirk and Hibernian, and with Celtic just a point clear of Rangers, he is indeed invaluable.
Despite his late header giving the thousands of travelling Celtic fans a thrilling end to a relatively turgid game, the intervention is another significant moment in a season that is threatening to unravel if individual performances fail to continue papering over glaring deficiencies across the park.
If the lively Jota - who lasted 74 minutes - was not creating chances, tormenting full-backs or digging out enticing crosses in the first half, Celtic seemed without any real plan of attack.
Yang and Luke McCowan's involvements were limited at best, Hogh's chance to stake a claim was sub-par to be kind, and there was no driving force from the middle of the park to show some impetus.
Arithmetically, Celtic can still finish in any position in the Europa League table. But if they are to claim a playoff or automatic qualification spot, they will need Duran to remain in such a rich vein of form.
What are the fans saying?
Brian: Embarrassed by that performance, I know that there no easy games in Europe, couldn't pass the ball, not fit enough, no style of play and poorly coached. The club is in decline.
John: Celtic are just an average side these days - there should be no expectation.
Ted: That was just embarrassing. The 31st team in Portugal made us look ordinary. Go now Martin with dignity intact and preserve your achievements. Thus mob will drag you down.
Allan: Outclassed and out paced by Torreense, Celtic played poorly with a lot of comedy of errors in their play. But Yippee hee, Celtic. Won with a late goal from Duran.
Liam: This can't go on any further now, regardless of the result. MON is done and the coaching staff are done. Booing substitutions is the end, never mind a performance like this against second division opposition. The board can resign too.
Alec: Total embarrassment. Barring Jota, there was a complete lack of creativity, quality, urgency and belief. Time for the board to make the right decisions, get a new manager in and get rid of at least 10 of those players on show tonight.

Send us your views on Celtic

items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
items.summary: Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. items.text:
Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. Simon Burnton
Nottingham Forest v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times GMT)
When Leeds recruited Dominic Calvert-Lewin on a free transfer during the summer of 2025 it is fair to say many of their fans were underwhelmed. Now though the news that the England centre-forward has penned a contract extension at Elland Road is a cause for celebration in West Yorkshire. Calvert-Lewin had proved somewhat injury-prone at his former club, Everton, yet Daniel Farke evidently knew what he was doing. The newly robust 29-year-old has scored 18 goals in 46 Premier League appearances for Leeds, 17 arriving in the last 36 games. With Calvert-Lewin now having signed a new, improved deal extending until 2029, attention is turning to Farke’s own contract. The German’s current agreement expires next summer but renewal talks have been under way for some time and, for the moment at least, the normally open Leeds manager has turned coy. “I’ve fallen in love with the club,” said Farke ahead of his upwardly mobile team’s home meeting with Coventry. “But I’m not willing to speak about my future.” Louise Taylor
Leeds v Coventry, Saturday 3pm
Mauricio Pochettino will send out his first Manchester United XI at Old Trafford on Saturday hoping Senne Lammens’ errors for the season are over. The fumble of a simple aerial ball late on at Sporting that allowed Luis Suárez to salvage a point on Wednesday was dismal from the goalkeeper despite his head coach’s protestations that the backline as a collective was at fault for allowing the opening. Karl Darlow, United’s second choice, has Premier League experience after a stint as Leeds’ first choice towards the end of last season but has played only 30 games in all divisions in the past three years. That means, probably, that Pochettino will retain Lammens but if more mistakes follow then the Wales international Darlow may be handed his chance. Jamie Jackson
Manchester United v Brentford, Saturday 3pm
Being forced from the field with “stud marks all the way down the back of his calf” after a clash with Tottenham’s Mohammed Kudus towards the end of last weekend’s match led to Leif Davis missing his first Premier League minutes of the season. It left Ipswich’s central defensive pairing of Issa Diop and Dara O’Shea as their only players to have been on the pitch for the entirety of the league campaign so far. O’Shea said this week of playing with Diop that “the more games we play with each other, obviously the better we’ll become as a pair”. They’re being given the best possible chance, even if Ipswich are yet to keep a clean sheet and have already conceded 22 goals, from an opposition xG of 21.82. Only the league’s bottom two have conceded a higher xG. More surprising is that Aston Villa have the next highest tally, with 18.56. Tuesday, when Villa lost 1-0 at Galatasaray, marked out a month since their last win. They have drawn three and scored in only two of their six outings. Ipswich may be just two points and two places outside the bottom three, but a win would put these teams level. SB
Ipswich v Aston Villa, Saturday 5.30pm
“We are having a great week,” Virgil van Dijk said after Liverpool followed up their 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United with a 3-0 win at Club Brugge that reinforced the strides being made by Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Andoni Iraola’s team overall. Liverpool’s week contrasts starkly with their local rivals. Everton suffered the heaviest defeat and produced arguably the worst performance of David Moyes’s second spell in charge on Monday when going down 4-0 at Brentford. James Tarkowski’s red card made no difference, so superior were Keith Andrews’s side from the start, but the absence of the Everton captain could be keenly felt on Sunday. Liverpool won the first Merseyside derby at Hill Dickinson Stadium last season from a 100th-minute corner, capitalising on disruption to Everton’s central defence when Jarrad Branthwaite went off injured. Without Tarkowski the hosts may be vulnerable again. Jake O’Brien could get his long-awaited chance to stake a claim as Branthwaite’s partner in the most demanding circumstances. Andy Hunter
Everton v Liverpool, Sunday noon
Georginio Rutter offered an insight into the Fabian Hürzeler effect at Brighton this week. “He has changed the mentality of some of the players: he wants us to run and give 100% – we did that last season but not as hard as he wanted,” said the Frenchman. “Some new players have come in and given us a new vibe.” While the likes of Luka Vuskovic – who surpassed Rutter as Brighton’s record signing in the summer – and Chema Andrés have quickly established themselves as first choices, the 24-year-old forward who joined from Leeds in 2024 has fallen behind Greek teenager Charalampos Kostoulas since recovering from a foot injury. Hearts' European hopes hang by a thread but Vrancken proud
- Published
There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.
Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to
items.text:
Hearts' European hopes hang by a thread but Vrancken proud
- Published
There was a bittersweet feeling at Tynecastle after Folarin Balogun's 94th-minute winner preserved Monaco's perfect Conference League record and condemned Hearts to a third defeat from four.
Wouter Vrancken's side had gone toe-to-toe with one of the best teams in the tournament, scored two glorious goals, but ultimately came away with nothing for their efforts.
Now they have little to no margin for error in their two remaining league phase matches.
They will likely have to beat both Borac Banja Luka of Bosnia and Cyprus' Pafos to reach the knockout stages, but if they perform as they did against Monaco, they will give themselves a fighting chance.
Hearts have garnered a reputation as entertainers under Vrancken - scoring a raft of goals while being porous at the back.
This game was their season in microcosm. The goals - scored by Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota - were things of beauty, picture-perfect strikes worthy of any stage.
But as thrilling as Hearts were in attack, they were as baffling at the back.
Jamie McCart unnecessarily tripped Matthis Abline, allowing Balogun to score from the penalty spot and Monaco's second came from Altena giving the ball away.
"It's Gladiators - are we not entertained? It's sensational," said Hearts legend John Robertson at half-time, with the game finely poised at 2-2.
'Biggest thing is pride in performance'
Both teams had chances to win it in the second half, but it was Monaco who took theirs in the final stages. Mamadou Coulibaly was afforded too much space and he slipped Balogun through to beat Beau Reus.
"It's a lack of nous and a little bit of naivety," former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart said on TNT Sports. "McCart backs off and allows the ball to be played into Balogun's feet."
Despite the frustrating nature of the late concession, Vrancken's overwhelming emotion was of pride.
"I'm very disappointed with how we give the goal away at the end," he said.
"The biggest thing is the pride for the performance today. Against a side of Monaco's [quality] - we're still missing nine players through injury - this performance was really pleasing."
Before the recent international break, Hearts were beaten 3-1 by Swiss outfit Thun, before a shock 5-2 home defeat by high-flying Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership.
However, they bounced back with a ruthless 8-0 win at Dundee on Saturday and carried that confidence into this game against a team with a far bigger budget.
"You saw that the confidence was there from the weekend and there was conviction around their box," Vrancken added. "It will not work every time, but the conviction and energy was there again.
"Our team kept their heads in the game and kept going for it, not being pleased with 2-2. Really pleased with what I saw."
Aside from his dismay at Balogun's winner and how it came about, Vrancken's main gripe was with the officials.
He felt there was a foul on Kerjota in the build-up to Monaco's second goal and was bemused at the fact neither Takumi Minamino and Denis Zakaria were sent off.
Minamino - already on a yellow card - wiped out Sabri Guendouz on the edge of the Monaco box, but got away with a warning. And VAR opted not to intervene after Zakaria went over the top of the ball and caught Pierre Landry Kabore on the shin.
"The second goal, they pulled Sabah [Kerjota] and he can't do his defensive work," Vrancken said.
"It was not the only refereeing decision that was interesting tonight. I don't know how it's possible not to give a red card for the tackle on [Pierre Landry Kabore]. It's clearly above the ankle, so it's always a red card.
"And why didn't Minamino get a second yellow before half-time? He prevents a shot from Sabri at the edge of the box.
"The explanation of the fourth official was even more crazy - he explained it could be for his first yellow card, but not for his second yellow. It was clearly a yellow card and then we were against 10 in the second half."

Send us your views on Hearts

items.title: 'Game of their lives': USWNT expects tough El Salvador test with WC at stake
items.summary:
MANSFIELD, Texas -- United States women's national team head coach Emma Hayes said she expects El Salvador to play "the game of their lives" in Friday's Concacaf W Championship quarterfinal.
The winner will automatically qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.
"I always respect every oppon
items.text:
MANSFIELD, Texas -- United States women's national team head coach Emma Hayes said she expects El Salvador to play "the game of their lives" in Friday's Concacaf W Championship quarterfinal.
The winner will automatically qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.
"I always respect every opponent, and you have to start with that," Hayes told reporters on Thursday at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium. "I think if you start looking at things like rankings, then you prime your brain to say things like, 'Oh, it's going to be an easy game.'
"More often than not, from my experiences, they end up being more challenging for lots of reasons. First of all, for El Salvador, this is going to be the game of their lives. They get the opportunity to qualify for the World Cup."
El Salvador are ranked No. 78 in the world and making their first appearance at the Concacaf W Championship after winning their pre-qualifying group.
The United States has qualified for all nine previous Women's World Cups and won four of them, more than any other country. The Americans are ranked second in the world behind Spain and are one of the contenders to win the 2027 edition. They are also the reigning Olympic champions.
"They have a lot of pride, and they want to perform for their country," Hayes said about El Salvador. "There's something at stake, and because of that, it's not a friendly game. And disrupting a team like the United States it might not be going toe-to-toe with us in certain parts of the game, but making it difficult for us? One hundred percent I think that will be the case."
Hayes praised El Salvador's ability to create opportunities in counterattacks and one-v-one opportunities. She also pointed to El Salvador's threat on set pieces.
Earlier in the day at training, U.S. captain Lindsey Heaps told ESPN and a small group of reporters that there is more game footage of Concacaf opponents than in previous cycles, which allows for more specific preparation.
Heaps echoed Hayes, saying that "we do not take any of these games lightly," and that the team prepared for El Salvador like they did for matches against world No. 1 Spain last month.
U.S. forward Sophia Wilson said that each game is like a final, which is good preparation for the World Cup.
"Any Concacaf tournament, we know it's going to be a challenge in a different way," Wilson said. "It's going to be maybe a little bit of a chaotic game, but I think that's a good test for us."
Hayes told reporters at Saturday's NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., that she was excited to finally have the opportunity to start the self-proclaimed "Triple Espresso" of Wilson, Trinity Rodman and Mallory Swanson together for the first time since the 2024 Olympics.
About an hour later, in the opening minutes of the Washington Spirit's 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current, Rodman was tackled hard and injured her shoulder.
Rodman stayed in the match and scored the Spirit's lone goal in second-half stoppage time. She said after the game that her shoulder felt "phenomenal," but U.S. Soccer announced earlier this week that Rodman would miss World Cup qualifying. She was replaced on the roster by forward Jaedyn Shaw.
"For Trin, she took a pretty hard hit," Hayes said on Thursday. "She was pretty beat up after the game. This happens, and unfortunately, she's not fit for this camp, but I'm sure she will be back by January."
Also absent from the U.S. roster is forward and attacking midfielder Pietra Tordin, who earned her first call-up and first cap last month against Spain. Tordin is training with Brazil in Japan during this international window. She holds dual citizenship with the U.S. and Brazil and has played for both countries at the youth international level.
"She was with us, and obviously she's got Brazilian heritage.," Hayes said. "She's going to train with Brazil. No more than that, so she's not cap-tied. I understand. It was a conversation that I've had, particularly with her agent, and yeah, there's no more to be said on it."
El Salvador's federation announced earlier this week that it would pay the players a $1 million shared bonus if they qualify for the World Cup for the first time.
The losers of the four Concacaf quarterfinals will get second chances at qualification in play-in games next week. The two winners of those matches will advance to next year's FIFA global playoff, where the final World Cup berths will be secured.
"Process is a really, really, really heavy word," El Salvador head coach Erick Acuña told reporters on Friday. "We are just trying to go step by step. And every step that we made, we have to be really secure. But we don't want to dream; we want to do.
"At the end of everything, we have to believe in step by step, because I don't want to be lucky. I just want to be secure that we are going to be in these stages all the time, and the only way to do it is believe. We have to believe in our process but inside of the process, there's a lot of things that we have to do. We have to invest. Without investment, there is no progression."

items.title: Bournemouth set new English record in Europe with 5th straight win
items.summary:
Bournemouth's dream Europa League start continued on Thursday as the south-coast club set a new record for a debuting English club in Europe.
Marco Rose's side fought back from a goal down in Spain against Celta Vigo to win 2-1 and extend their perfect start to the competition to five games.
- Europ
items.text:
Bournemouth's dream Europa League start continued on Thursday as the south-coast club set a new record for a debuting English club in Europe.
Marco Rose's side fought back from a goal down in Spain against Celta Vigo to win 2-1 and extend their perfect start to the competition to five games.
- Europa League game halted amid police clashes over fans' Palestine banner
They are the first English club in history to win their first five European games and are only the third team ever in major European competitions to achieve that feat, after Nürnberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.
It was also a club-record extending 10th straight win in all competitions for Marco Rose's side, who sit an impressive fifth in the Premier League.
Thursday's win, which keeps them top of the Europa League league phase table, was made all the more impressive by the fact it came after playing for more than an hour with 10 men following Bafodé Diakité's red card in the 23rd minute.
"We showed a lot of character," Bournemouth's Amine Adli TNT Sport. "It's amazing to come back in this way and go back home with the three points.
"I think it was down to the mentality of the players. From the moment we conceded the goal, and even after the red card, we always believed in ourselves.
"What's fantastic is that in the dressing room, even before the coach started speaking, everybody was saying, 'we can do this.' Everyone was motivated and still believed we could turn things around."
Adli's cross shortly after time set up Álvaro Rodríguez to head an equalising goal, turning the tables on Celta after they had gone in at halftime a goal up and a man up.
"I was looking for someone in the box," Adli added. "I know Alvaro is very good in the air and he was in a good position so I just tried to deliver a dangerous ball towards the far post."
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Rodríguez's goal then set the tone for an excellent second half in which Rose's team were comfortably the better side despite their numerical disadvantage.
Substitute Rayan swept in the winner 12 minutes from time to give Bournemouth one foot into the knockout rounds.
Information from ESPN Global Research and PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Kimmich slams 'not Bayern-like' treatment of Musiala amid health row
items.summary:
Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused
items.text:
Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO.
Now a key player has spoken out, too, and warned Bayern risks undermining its family image.
"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday.
"It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either."
Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's run of injuries over the last two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, had more impact on his game than the neurological condition.
"It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.
Bayern met with Musiala's agents Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension.
Bayern said the club and Musiala's representatives both accept he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension.
"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said.
Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the field in two preseason games, leaving players and fans alarmed.
- Bayern Munich, Jamal Musiala mess shows German champs at their worst
- Bayern Munich: Jamal Musiala's health 'top priority' amid contract doubts
- Injury-hit Bayern beaten by Lille to suffer first UCL loss
Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue.
Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern's loss at Lille, which continued a bad week for Bayern.
Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga to Borussia Dortmund and have now slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings.

items.title: Europa League game halted amid police clashes over fans' Palestine banner
items.summary:
BATUMI, Georgia -- The UEFA Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestinians.
The game, being played on neutral ground in Batu
items.text:
BATUMI, Georgia -- The UEFA Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestinians.
The game, being played on neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia, was halted in the 26th minute but restarted after the interruption and was eventually won 2-1 by Besiktas.
Turkey's Haberturk broadcaster said Georgian police used pepper spray against the Besiktas fans, who also unfurled a Palestinian flag, prompting the referee to stop the game with the score 0-0.
In a statement, Besiktas accused the Georgian security forces of using "disproportionate" force against supporters before and during the game.
"We strongly condemn the security forces for their use of disproportionate force against our fans," the club said. "We also extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our fans affected by these incidents."
The Turkish Football Federation condemned the treatment of Besiktas supporters on X, saying they were subjected to unacceptable behavior and discrimination. It said it would press for an investigation.
Earlier, the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, the state-run Anadolu Agency reported.
UEFA relocated the match after Turkish authorities said Istanbul could not host it for safety and security reasons.
Unlike two previous Hapoel away games, spectators were allowed in the stadium.

items.title: Thanksgiving delight: USMNT star Pulisic nets vital Milan winner
items.summary:
Christian Pulisic enjoyed a Thanksgiving to remember as the United States star came off the bench to help fuel AC Milan's 4-2 comeback win at Olympiacos in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday.
Despite Milan coach Ruben Amorim describing Pulisic in recent days as the one player his side could not repl
items.text:
Christian Pulisic enjoyed a Thanksgiving to remember as the United States star came off the bench to help fuel AC Milan's 4-2 comeback win at Olympiacos in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday.
Despite Milan coach Ruben Amorim describing Pulisic in recent days as the one player his side could not replace, the attacker was named among the substitutes for the game in Greece.
With Milan trailing 1-0 at halftime, Amorim turned to Pulisic in an attempt to spark a second-half revival. The 28-year-old delivered, volleying home a cross in the 71st minute for the eventual game winner.
As the home side chased an equalizer in the dying moments, Pulisic then laid on a simple fourth goal for Diego Moreira.
"It was a decisive game for us," Pulisic told Sky Sport Italia. "From today, every game is like a final. We didn't start well but we were much better in the second half. It's important to find this intensity."
Goals from Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cissè had earlier brought Milan level after an own goal from Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan and a goal from Jota Silva had put Olympiacos in front 2-0.
Pulisic, who scored in both legs of the U.S. men's national team's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal win over Haiti earlier this month, has now scored in his past five games for club and country. That streak is tied for the best of Pulisic's career, matching his run in September 2024.
After Milan lost three of their first four games in this season's Europa League, Thursday's win could prove vital to their hopes of advancing to the knockout stage.
"It changed our future," Amorim said. "It's completely different to win this game or lose this game. We did well in the second half but we [made] a lot of mistakes again."
Following a low-key start at the Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis, Olympiacos broke the deadlock from a corner in the 31st minute.
Former Inter defender Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header against the crossbar and the ball bounced back into the net off Maignan's arm.
Olympiacos, who were unbeaten in Europe with three wins, scored again four minutes into the second half.
Remo Freuler found Jota Silva at the edge of the penalty area and Silva fired the ball past Maignan into the top corner.
Milan got themselves back into the match through a fine individual goal from Hutchinson in the 56th minute.
The on-loan Nottingham Forest winger picked the ball up on the halfway line and burst down the right before cutting inside at the edge of the penalty area and rolling the ball into the far corner.
The Rossoneri struck again in the 63rd minute, when Hutchinson sent over a cross from the right toward the back post, where Cissè nodded the ball past Olympiacos keeper Stefan Ortega.
Pulisic completed the turnaround with 20 minutes left when he volleyed home a cross from the right after more quick footwork from Hutchinson.
Moreira swept home a fourth in added time following a swift counterattack by Pulisic.
Information from PA contributed to this report.

items.title: USWNT's Coffey grateful for 'surreal' return for Women's World Cup qualifying
items.summary:
DALLAS -- Midfielder Sam Coffey said it is "surreal" to return to the United States women's national team for World Cup qualifying after missing recent major matches due to injuries.
Coffey is back with the U.S. for the first time since April after undergoing a minor knee procedure in May. She said
items.text:
DALLAS -- Midfielder Sam Coffey said it is "surreal" to return to the United States women's national team for World Cup qualifying after missing recent major matches due to injuries.
Coffey is back with the U.S. for the first time since April after undergoing a minor knee procedure in May. She said that the time she missed made her even more grateful to be part of the USWNT.
"I try to never take this environment for granted," Coffey told ESPN and a small group of reporters at training on Thursday. "I feel like that has multiplied now since going through a few injuries this year after not really experiencing that in my career thus far.
"I always have such gratitude for being here, and I think that just is even more so true now. It feels so good to be back and to be able to be here at this time, too, where it's such an important camp and the stakes are really big."
The U.S. plays El Salvador on Friday night in Mansfield, Texas, in the quarterfinals of the Concacaf W Championship. The winner of the match automatically qualifies for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.
The U.S. women have won four World Cups and never missed the final tournament in nine all-time editions.
Coffey was a spectator from TV for the United States' pair of away games against Brazil in June. Brazil and the U.S. split those results in physical, contentious matches.
Coffey also missed last month's friendly matches against world No. 1 Spain. She was on hand in the stadium for the second match in which the Americans rallied from 2-0 down to earn a 2-2 draw.
"It's always just a privilege and a joy to be here," Coffey said. "I think this year taught me so much about -- so many lessons in that. How much of a gift it is just to be playing and to be playing with the best team in the world, and how much I hated with all my heart missing those windows and being and home and not being able to contribute and be there with the girls.
"I think I just come in with a different perspective now, a bit of a reframe and a re-shift."
Coffey said she is "finding [her] rhythm" again in camp with the team in order to rebuild connections and pick up certain information from the coaching staff. She last played for the U.S. in April against Japan.
Coffey has made 46 career appearances for the USWNT and became an anchor for the team as a defensive midfielder in recent years, including starting during the team's run to a 2024 Olympic gold medal.
Being exposed to different styles of play in England, where she plays for Manchester City, has helped her game, Coffey said.
She added that her knee feels good and she feels physically healthy -- other than a small cold she caught recently.
Coffey was originally named to the USWNT's roster for the October matches against Spain but withdrew from camp after sustaining an ankle injury while playing for Manchester City.
She flew to the U.S. during the international window and watched the U.S. play Spain in Chester, Pennsylvania. What Coffey saw from the team was encouraging, she said.
"It just made me so excited and proud to see how we've progressed and just how good we are, and how we still have like those little last details that we need to fine-tune," Coffey said.

items.title: Europa League: Bournemouth make it a perfect 10 while Celtic leave it late
items.summary:
Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.
It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for t
items.text:
Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.
It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafodé Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Álvaro Rodríguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Rose’s team could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen, 4-0 winners over Benfica, in two weeks’ time.
Camilo Durán came to Celtic’s rescue in Europe again after coming off the bench to head a late winner against Torreense in Portugal.
The Colombian striker peeled off to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest and send a downward header into the net in the 85th minute. Durán’s 15th goal of the season earned a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and put Celtic on six points in the Europa League after his double off the bench inspired a comeback win over Besiktas last time out.
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vázquez sliced Jota’s cross into his own net with Yang Hyun-jun right behind him. But the Portuguese Cup winners levelled 10 minutes later after some sloppy defending. Both Kieran Tierney and Colby Donovan had chances to deal with bouncing balls after Álex Alfaro hit the bar from 22 yards but they could not clear and Haiti international Dany Jean volleyed home.
Celtic dominated second-half possession but clear chances were at a premium until Durán struck. Torreense sit 13th in the Portuguese second tier and hosted Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home town. Hoops fans formed the vast majority of the 4,971 crowd. But the hosts started the game three points ahead of Celtic after wins over Lillestrøm and Ararat-Armenia, and they had taken the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.
The lead-up to Marseille against Levski Sofia was marred by incidents in the stands between supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered.
Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. “Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” the Marseille police prefecture said. Six others were treated on site for various wounds. The home team went on to win the game 1-0 thanks to a first-half Amine Gouiri penalty.
Ruben Amorim’s Milan gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos.
Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knockout phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Jota Silva’s 49th-minute strike. Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the winger then set up Alphadjo Cissé to equalise in the 63rd minute.
Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth.
Juventus shrugged off an early scare to cruise past Cypriots Omonia Nicosia and move closer to confirming a top-eight place in the Europa League with a 4-1 win in Turin.
The Italian giants fell behind to a 15th-minute strike from Lubomir Satka but levelled through Andrea Cambiaso before further goals from Jeff Ekhator, Francisco Conceiçao and Jeremie Boga earned a comfortable win. Only Bournemouth sit above Juve in the table.
Bayer Leverkusen also remained in contention for automatic progression after second-half strikes from Malik Tillman and Jarell Quansah secured a 2-0 win at Dinamo Zagreb. Hoffenheim secured their second win in this season’s competition by beating Sturm Graz 3-1.

items.title: With World Cup qualification at stake, the USWNT has no excuses
items.summary:
The task for the U.S. women's national team is simple: one win and they're in for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
On paper, Concacaf's revamped qualification format looks even easier for the USWNT: As the region's top team and the FIFA No. 2-ranked team in the world, the USWNT faces El Salvador, the tea
items.text:
The task for the U.S. women's national team is simple: one win and they're in for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
On paper, Concacaf's revamped qualification format looks even easier for the USWNT: As the region's top team and the FIFA No. 2-ranked team in the world, the USWNT faces El Salvador, the team ranked No. 78 in the world, in the tournament quarterfinal on Friday in Mansfield, Texas.
Naturally, USWNT head coach Emma Hayes is not taking the bait.
"For us as a whole, Concacaf is a very different competition," Hayes told reporters on Saturday in Washington, D.C. "... These are the games where you say to yourself, 'Oh, you know, this is an easier opponent.' Let me be clear about this: This will be a very, very tough game. You have to prepare in the right way possible, and I will absolutely be making sure our group is switched on when they come in. It's really important."
Concacaf simplified its final phase of qualifying to be a single-elimination tournament after FIFA reduced the number of international match windows. The four winners of the quarterfinals on Friday and Saturday will advance to the 2027 World Cup, while the losers will go into a play-in bracket to advance to the global playoff. In other words: if the U.S. advances vs. El Salvador on Friday, the rest of the Concacaf tournament doesn't matter -- the USA's World Cup spot will have been clinched.
With all due respect to the rest of the field, the Americans' toughest opponent could be themselves.
Health and fatigue are factors. Eighteen of the 23 players on the USWNT roster for qualifying compete in the NWSL, which just wrapped up its grueling eight-months season on Saturday. Forward Trinity Rodman has already been removed from the World Cup qualifying roster after sustaining a shoulder injury in the opening minutes of the Washington Spirit's 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship.
Without a doubt, there are other U.S. players carrying knocks or heavy legs following the NWSL season. Several of them, like midfielder Rose Lavelle, played more limited roles in the NWSL playoffs as they managed health issues. They must all quickly switch from club to international duties.
"Get used to it -- that's the realities of it," Hayes said.
And, as usual, this FIFA window comes immediately after the NWSL Championship -- except this time it for World Cup qualifying, not a set of friendlies like in previous years.
"There is no such thing as a friendly," Hayes said when asked about the difference in approach to this window. "It's a terrible term. They need to get rid of it. Every game is a competitive game, and if you don't train like it's your World Cup final and play games like that, how can you expect to perform at that level? For me, it's no different than the other games that we play, except we have the opportunity to qualify for something. That's the only difference."
In theory, Concacaf's updated qualifying format is more difficult. Single-elimination knockout games typically give less talented teams a greater chance at an upset as opposed to round-robin or group-stage tournaments in which teams need consistent results to advance.
Concacaf has reverted from its previous format ahead of the 2023 World Cup, when two groups of four played in the 100-degree daily heat of Monterrey, Mexico, for four automatic bids and two berths in FIFA's global playoff. The outcome was thrilling and entertaining by the standards of Concacaf tournaments: Concacaf ultimately maxed out its potential World Cup berths at six (and Jamaica was the most impressive member nation at the 2026 World Cup), and somehow hosts Mexico were one of the two teams that did not advance at all.
However, the changes to FIFA's international calendar and fixture congestion led to another simplified, single-elimination tournament. Concacaf created more meaningful games in the buildup to the final stage of qualifying, to develop teams and provide more meaningful games of consequence for more teams. Canada and the U.S. are joined by the six group-stage winners, including El Salvador, in the quarterfinals.
The four winners of the quarterfinals will advance to the 2027 World Cup, while the losers will go into a play-in bracket to advance to the global playoff. Three teams will also qualify for the 2028 Olympics alongside the U.S., who will host the Games.
The reality for the USWNT is that qualifying is almost always a formality. The only time that was not true was 16 years ago, when the U.S. women lost a Concacaf semifinal to Mexico in Cancun in the biggest upset in program history. The Americans were ranked No. 1 in the world but had to then go beat Italy in a two-leg playoff to qualify as the 16th and final team for the 2011 World Cup.
Those stories -- the raucous crowd in Mexico, Abby Wambach getting her head stapled in the final minutes of the game, a young Alex Morgan saving the U.S. in the first leg in Italy -- were passed on across generations of players so that the mistake would not be repeated.
El Salvador is even less likely to pull off an upset than that talented Mexico team from 16 years ago.
Friday's quarterfinal will be played in suburban Dallas, for one. Poorly promoted Concacaf games don't have the crowds of U.S. Soccer-hosted or FIFA-hosted ones, but the home field advantage will go to the U.S., if anyone.
El Salvador have their own problems, too. The team was in turmoil a month ago when its coach, Eric Acuña, made comments to reporters questioning his players' commitment and threatening to revoke their basic rights to do things like getting coffee during training camp. Acuña also publicly criticized his players, who responded strongly to rebuke their coach.
The El Salvadorian federation released a statement condemning Acuña's comments and supporting the players, but the coach remains in charge for qualifying.
El Salvador's federation released a statement on Tuesday saying that the 23 players on the World Cup qualifying roster will share a $1 milli

items.title: How USWNT can qualify for World Cup, matchups, format
items.summary:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is approaching quickly, but there are still plenty of spots up for grabs in the sport's biggest tournament.
Four of those places will be decided at the Concacaf W Championship, where the United States, Canada and Mexico are among the participating teams.
Here's everything
items.text:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is approaching quickly, but there are still plenty of spots up for grabs in the sport's biggest tournament.
Four of those places will be decided at the Concacaf W Championship, where the United States, Canada and Mexico are among the participating teams.
Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming tournament.
- How teams can qualify for 2027 Women's World Cup
When is the Concacaf W Championship?
The tournament begins Nov. 27 and concludes with the final on Dec. 5. All matches will take place in Houston and Mansfield, Texas.
What is the format?
The Concacaf W Championship is essentially a straight knockout tournament between eight qualifying teams. (The two highest-ranked teams in the FIFA Women's World Ranking as of Aug. 7 -- the United States and Canada -- earned safe passage to the W Championship, while the remaining teams had to win their groups in the qualifying round.)
The teams were seeded according to their FIFA ranking and placed in a bracket, with the No. 1 seed facing No. 8, No. 2 paired with No. 7, and so on. Winners in the quarterfinals advance to the semifinals, and the winning semifinal teams will contest the final.
Here are the matchups in the quarterfinal round:
No. 1 United States vs. No. 8 El Salvador (Nov. 27, 8:30 p.m. ET)
No. 4 Jamaica vs. No. 5 Costa Rica (Nov. 27, 5 p.m. ET)
No. 2 Canada vs. No. 7 Panama (Nov. 28, 1 p.m. ET)
No. 3 Mexico vs. No. 6 Haiti (Nov. 28, 4:30 p.m. ET)
How do teams qualify for the Women's World Cup?
Quite simply, the four teams that win in the quarterfinals will qualify for the Women's World Cup. For the U.S. women, that means a win against El Salvador on Nov. 27 will send them through to the World Cup.
If a team loses in the quarterfinals, can they still qualify?
Yes -- the losing teams will compete in play-in matches for the interconfederation playoffs, which conclude in February. Those playoffs will determine the final qualifiers for the World Cup.
Which teams are the favorites to win it all?
The United States remains the powerhouse in Concacaf. The winner in nine of the past 11 editions of this tournament (as well as four-time World Cup champions), coach Emma Hayes' team is firmly expected to steamroll its way to the final.
Canada might have something to say about that, though. Its FIFA ranking of ninth signals the threat they pose; boasting young stars such as Arsenal's Olivia Smith and veterans Jessie Fleming and Kadeisha Buchanan, Canada is capable of pushing the U.S. to the limit.
Who are the USWNT players to watch?
The United States' 51-player preliminary roster for the tournament was trimmed down to 23 and finalized on Nov. 18. Forwards Trinity Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Sophia Wilson are among the players hoping to get on the scoresheet, while experienced midfielders Rose Lavelle and Lindsey Heaps will look to control the center of the pitch.
OL Lyonnes' Lily Yohannes could also make a big impact. The highly regarded 19-year-old midfielder scored a stunning strike from long range in the UEFA Women's Champions League back in October.
One notable player who wasn't named to the team is Chelsea center back Naomi Girma, who has been out with a muscle injury since early October.
